#1757. GdS: Unbeaten and hope or room for error – Milan begin Europa League calculations

AC Milan have four games left to play in the Europa League and they’re in the do-or-die stage of the competition already.

Thoughts on the Europa League this season were mixed. On paper, Milan should have been competing at the top. Yet, they’ve struggled through the League Phase so far, leaving themselves with something of a mountain to climb, starting against Olympiacos later this week.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, the Rossoneri are in a more-than-difficult position. Sitting 28th in the rankings, they are currently outside the qualification spots and calculations are difficult to make about how much they’ll need to improve.

From the past two seasons, they’ll need between 14 and 16 points to qualify for the top eight, which feels like a distant hope. If they’re to achieve that amount, they must win all four of their remaining games and hope that 15 is enough.

The play-offs, on the other hand, are more than feasible. Sitting four places off currently, there’s a one-point gap to overturn and history says they’ll need either nine or 10 points. This would allow far more room for error, with only two wins and a draw needed to ‘guarantee’ a spot in the next round.

In Greece, they’ll face the first hurdle and getting three points would make life much easier for everyone involved.

#1756. Auxerre vs Marseille - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 27 Nov 2026 02:00

Auxerre will try to put some more distance between themselves and the relegation zone as they wrap up November by welcoming Marseille to Stade de l’Abbe-Deschamps on Sunday.

After 11 matchdays, the Burgundy club sit 15th in the Ligue 1 table, drawing Monaco 1-1 the last time out, with OM currently in fifth following to a 3-2 defeat at Le Mans.

After a rough start to the 2026-27 campaign, it appears as though Auxerre are doing just enough to get by domestically.

Will Still’s men lost their first three matches of this top-flight season, but have since collected points in six of their last eight league fixtures.

That has them just a point above Strasbourg who are in the relegation playoff spot heading into matchday 12 with Auxerre just three points above Angers, who are in the last automatic relegation position.

So far this season AJA have yet to lose a Ligue 1 fixture when netting the opening goal, with their draw versus Monaco last week being the first time they dropped points in that position.

They lead the league regarding fouls per match (16.1) while allowing the joint-most goals in this competition after 11 matchdays (25).

AJA have points in three of their last four Ligue 1 fixtures at home, with their last win at Stade de l’Abbe-Deschamps occuring in September against Brest (2-1).

Marseille will hope their late collapse against Le Mans serves as a temporary speed bump and a wake-up call going forward.

Bruno Genesio’s side bounced back well in midweek, defeating Levski Sofia 1-0 in Europa League action, putting them into the knockout places in that competition.

Clean sheets like the one they collected on Thursday have been rare for OM in Ligue 1, as they have conceded a 2.40 xG average following their defeat to Le Mans in the top flight.

Fortunately, they are balancing that out with plenty of goals, averaging the second-most goals per game in Ligue 1 (2.2) heading into matchday 12.

After 11 matchdays, only three points currently separate them from the top three and a place in next season’s Champions League.

Les Olympiens will seek a third successive triumph versus Auxerre in this competition, having won both Ligue 1 meetings against them last season 1-0.

Both Bryan Okoh and Assane Diousse will miss this match for Auxerre as they recover from cruciate ligament tears, while Sekou Fofana has a groin strain and Danny Loader is questionable with an ankle injury.

Romain Faivre scored their only goal on matchday 11, the second of the campaign for the man currently on loan from Bournemouth.

At Marseille, Derek Cornelius is still recovering from a hip problem, Emerson Palmieri is questionable with a knee injury and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg is questionable because of an illness.

Amine Gouiri scored the winner in their Europa League victory on Thursday, becoming the first OM player to net in five successive competitive fixtures since Florian Thauvin in 2018, while he and Igor Paixao scored in their defeat to Le Mans.

Nardi; Diomande, Tuanzebe, Siwe; Senaya, Ahamada, Danois, Oppegard; Faivre, Lascary; Archer

De Lange; Weah, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia; Kamissoko, Nnadi; Gomes, Maupay, Paixao; Gouiri

These are two of the most inconsistent defensive units in the league, and in a match which could be wide open for that reason, we believe the quality of the visitors, who have fared well in those kinds of matches this season, will enable them to prevail.

#1754. OLIVER HOLT: Man United ARE in a relegation battle - anybody who denies it is deluding themselves - and Mauricio Pochettino is already showing signs of cracking under pressure

Published: 07:54 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:31 EST, 23 November 2026

Early on in On the Road, somewhere between Chicago and Denver, Jack Kerouac described the journey his main character was taking and some of the trepidation that came with each new horizon. ‘I was halfway across America,’ he wrote, ‘at the dividing line between the East of my youth and the West of my future.’

Late on Sunday afternoon, as winter’s grey light turned to darkness on Merseyside and a bitter wind blew in off the Irish Sea, Manchester United’s new boss, Mauricio Pochettino, freshly arrived from Cincinnati, Ohio, arms folded grimly and tightly across his chest, stood on the touchline at Anfield and realised the full extent of what he had just got himself into.

Sure, the United job was too big to turn down. However far the club has fallen, it still has that lure. It still has the name, even if the name is now just one of those building facades on a film set.

There is the name and then there is the nothingness that is concealed beyond the name. There is the mismanaged, mistreated void that United has become.

And now United need to find out which version of Pochettino they have purchased. Because he is at a dividing line, too. Do they have the Pochettino who blazed a trail across the football landscape with Espanyol, Southampton and Spurs, although he did not win trophies at any of those destinations?

Or do they have the Pochettino whose reputation gradually became becalmed at Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the USA national team? They better hope they can restart something in him because this is the biggest and the hardest job Pochettino has ever had and it will take a Herculean effort just to survive.

Do Man United have the Mauricio Pochettino who blazed a trail with Espanyol, Southampton and Spurs? Or do they have the Pochettino whose reputation has fluctuated since?

That is what this season is about now for these fallen, ruined giants. It is about survival. Nothing more. If Pochettino did not realise it before, he will have realised it during that calamitous 4-0 defeat at Anfield: United are in a relegation battle and anyone who denies that is deluding themselves.

That is just pride talking. The remnants of what pride remains at United, anyway.

Maybe it hasn’t quite seemed real until now. Just like the prospect of Leicester City winning the Premier League didn’t start to feel real until around Christmas of 2015-16. United going down would be up there with Leicester winning the title in terms of seismic events in the modern English game. It’s time to start taking relegation seriously.

If you take the blinkers off for just a second, if you banish the muscle memory that tells you United are too successful and too rich to get sucked down into the Championship, then you have to accept that all the ingredients are there for United to get relegated. Take that name away and what’s left?

What’s left is a team that last won a Premier League game on August 30. What’s left is a team that has won one game all season. What’s left is a team that has conceded 34 goals across all competitions, more than any other team in Europe's top five leagues. What’s left is a team that has eight points from its first 11 league games.

Just for context, the Spurs side that spent most of last season haunted by the prospect of relegation, had 18 points at this stage of that campaign. If you still think the rabble currently representing the club are too good to go down, I think you are deluding yourself.

Yes, United played more than 80 minutes of the game against Liverpool with 10 men and, yes, the decision to send off Leny Yoro for his challenge on Alexander Isak was harsh. But the dismissal was also a fig-leaf for Pochettino and United. It was convenient. It was a disguise for what lay beneath.

United also brought it on themselves. Pochettino made one big selection decision before the game when he picked Matthijs de Ligt ahead of Harry Maguire. It was what former bosses in the English game might have described as a ‘big rick’. It was a terrible misjudgment.

Maybe the sending off of Leny Yoro was harsh. But United brought it on themselves

Matthijs de Ligt (right) was bullied by Alexander Isak at Anfield. Pochettino's decision to play the Dutchman was a terrible misjudgment

De Ligt’s first action was to watch a long ball from Ronald Araujo sail over his head, gazing at it with a mix of horror and wonder, as you might if you were watching the trajectory of an alien spaceship. Yoro was not quick enough to read De Ligt’s discomfort and so the horror ensued.

It was Pochettino’s first game and it is impossible to judge him yet but it is possible to say this was a bad start.

There were even a couple of worrying signs in his post-match press conference when the bonhomie and the relaxed demeanour that are among his great strengths deserted him.

When he was asked about United being in the relegation zone, he snapped that it was a ‘cheap’ question because he had only just arrived at the club. He said he saw fight in his players, which few others had seen. He blamed everything on the sending off of Yoro, even though it was his selection of De Ligt that had led to it.

A few alarm bells started to ring. Only faintly and only in the distance but they were ringing nonetheless. Pochettino has had big jobs before but he has never had a job as big as Manchester United where the scrutiny and the expectation and the judgment is relentless and unforgiving.

Pochettino has dealt with Daniel Levy at Spurs, which may not have been an easy relationship, but he has never dealt with a clown-show like the one that Jim Ratcliffe has put in place at Old Trafford.

United is rotten. Everyone can see that. Off the pitch, the club is at war with its own fans. The club gives every impression of trying to move on its most loyal supporters so that it can replace them with tourists and day-trippers who will spend more on tickets and in the club superstore and at the food stands.

‘The way you treat us is a disgrace,’ that banner in the Stretford End said a few weeks ago, and that is how the fans feel. They are more loyal than United deserve but their patience with their owners ran out a long time ago. Pochettino has a disaffected fanbase to deal with as well.

United is rotten on the pitch and it is rotten off the pitch. It feels as if the club is being slowly poisoned in plain sight. It feels as if it is getting weaker and weaker and weaker. And when Brentford arrive at Old Trafford next week, they will smell blood. Every club that comes to Old Trafford now smells blood.

Harry Maguire looks dejected at full-time on Sunday. United is rotten on the pitch and it is rotten off the pitch. It feels as if the club is being slowly poisoned in plain sight

Still think they’re too good to go down? Who are they better than in this league? Hull City? United don’t have the spirit of Hull City. They don’t have the togetherness. They don’t have the pride.

Hull got battered by Brighton on Sunday afternoon and still won 2-0. United could never have done that. United have already lost to Hull and Brighton this season, too.

So, yes, United are in a relegation fight. They’re one off the bottom of the league in the last week of November. Of course, they’re in a relegation fight. It’s on their new boss to get them out of it.

If Pochettino is on the wrong side of the dividing line of his career, if the best part of his journey is behind him, United are in big, big trouble.

#1753. Prediction: Hamburger SV vs Bayern Munich

Bayern Munich travel to the Volksparkstadion on Saturday aiming to put a difficult week behind them and reignite their Bundesliga title challenge against Hamburger SV.

The defending champions begin the weekend second in the table on 22 points, two behind leaders Borussia Dortmund, while Hamburg occupy 12th place with 12 points. Bayern will need a victory and a Dortmund slip-up if they are to end the round back at the summit.

Hamburg have generally enjoyed a positive campaign despite recent setbacks.

The Green-Whites have collected three more points after 10 Bundesliga matches than they managed at the same stage last season, evidence that progress is being made under Daniel Thioune.

However, results have taken a turn for the worse in recent weeks. Hamburg were heavily beaten 4-0 by Werder Bremen last weekend, and another defeat on Saturday could leave them just two points above the relegation zone.

Thioune’s side have now lost four of their last five matches in all competitions, scoring only five times while conceding 12 goals during that run. Those defensive struggles will be a major concern ahead of the visit of one of the division’s most dangerous attacking teams.

History also offers little encouragement. Hamburg have not beaten Bayern since July 2011, a sequence that has included 17 defeats and three draws.

Despite that record, home form has been respectable. HSV have won three of their five Bundesliga matches at the Volksparkstadion this season, although they have also suffered two defeats there.

Hamburg have been dealt a significant blow with midfielder Nicolai Remberg ruled out for the remainder of the season. His absence could see Nicolas Capaldo continue in central midfield.

In attack, Yussuf Poulsen is unavailable, meaning Patson Daka is expected to lead the line. He could be supported by Fabio Vieira, who is likely to feature in an advanced role.

Bayern arrive under unusual pressure after suffering their first defeat of the season.

The Bavarians were beaten 2-1 by Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday, a result that followed a disappointing 1-1 Bundesliga draw against FC Koln. Those results have raised concerns that Bayern could lose further ground in the title race if they fail to respond quickly.

The defeat in France was also Vincent Kompany’s second match back on the touchline following his collapse in October, and the Belgian coach is still attempting to guide his side through a difficult spell.

Despite their recent frustrations, Bayern remain one of the Bundesliga’s strongest sides statistically. They have scored 30 goals in just 10 league matches, while only Borussia Dortmund have conceded fewer than their tally of 10.

The champions’ loss to Lille was their first defeat in any competition this season and also their first away defeat. Before that setback, Bayern had won six and drawn three of their first nine away matches.

Off-field issues have also generated headlines, with criticism directed at the club hierarchy over their handling of Jamal Musiala’s health situation, prompting Joshua Kimmich to publicly support his teammate.

Star striker Harry Kane is expected to miss several months with an ankle injury, while Michael Olise is a doubt for the trip to Hamburg.

There is better news regarding Luis Diaz, who should be available in some capacity, although Bayern may still be forced to deploy natural midfielder Konrad Laimer as their central attacking option.

Aleksandar Pavlovic was used in a more advanced role against Lille because of Bayern’s attacking injury crisis, but he is expected to return to midfield alongside Joshua Kimmich this weekend.

Hamburg may feel they are catching Bayern at a favourable moment given the visitors’ injury list and recent drop in form. The absence of Harry Kane in particular removes a huge source of goals, while Kompany’s side are still recovering from their first defeat of the campaign.

Even so, Bayern possess significantly greater quality throughout the squad and remain one of the Bundesliga’s most potent attacking outfits. Hamburg’s defensive record in recent weeks is another concern, particularly against opposition capable of creating chances in volume.

The hosts should put up a fight, but Bayern are expected to respond positively to a difficult week and leave Hamburg with all three points.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

William Saliba is set to make his first-team return for Arsenal in the upcoming matches.

The Frenchman missed the first three months of the season with a back injury that he aggravated at the World Cup in the summer.

Although surgery was not needed, Saliba still required a lengthy period of rest and he is yet to play a single competitive minute for Mikel Arteta’s senior side this season.

He has, however, featured in a couple of behind-closed-doors friendly matches at Arsenal’s training ground. Saliba also played 45 minutes for the Under-21s before the recent international break.

The centre-back was included in the matchday squad against both Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund but remained an unused substitute on each occasion.

Arsenal have a relentless run of fixtures coming up before Christmas, including several huge matches. The Gunners host Manchester City on Sunday as they look to put a nine-point gap between the two clubs in the Premier League title race.

Arteta indicated that Saliba is unlikely to be thrown straight into the starting lineup against City, but could expect to feature very soon.

“Obviously he hasn’t played football for a long, long time,” Arteta said at his pre-match press conference on Friday.

“He can play a certain amount of minutes, so we need to be really, really sure. Especially in that kind of game when he comes in, that he can sustain a certain amount of minutes otherwise we’re not going to have enough subs or opportunities to make those subs.

“He’s training well, he will have minutes in the next few games. Then he will prove what he’s already done, which is that he’s an unbelievable player.”

Asked how many minutes Saliba was now capable of playing, Arteta added: “Now he’s got more training, another week or 10 days, that will extend.

“It will depend as well on the type of game and the exposure that he will have throughout the game.”

#1751. Chelsea transfer news: Blues 'closely monitor' Boca Juniors centre-back ahead of 2027

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 02:11

Chelsea are understood to be monitoring Boca Juniors centre-back Facundo Herrera after the defender’s swift emergence in South American football.

The 20-year-old, known in Argentina as ‘Jagger’ because of his likeness to Rolling Stones singer Mick Jagger, has made remarkable strides over the last four months.

After making his senior bow in August, the former captain of Boca’s reserve side swiftly established himself in the first team and helped the club win the Copa Sudamericana in Barranquilla last week.

Herrera impressed in the 2-0 final triumph over Atletico Mineiro, completing 56 of 58 passes and recording nine clearances as Boca kept a clean sheet.

Argentine publications El Crack Deportivo and Clarin via Sport Witness report that Chelsea scouts are closely assessing Herrera's physical and technical progress as part of the club’s continuing recruitment drive in South America.

The 1.80m right-footer has earned plaudits for his speed, aerial strength and composure when playing through the opposition’s press from the back.

Herrera showed his eye for a decisive moment on October 25 by scoring his first senior goal with a late winner against Independiente that secured Boca's place at the top of the annual league standings.

The youngster's growing standing has attracted praise from some of Argentina’s most respected figures: Boca's record appearance-maker Roberto Mouzo has likened him to 1978 World Cup winner Alberto Tarantini, while Oscar Ruggeri has called on national team manager Lionel Scaloni to give him senior minutes straight away.

Chelsea are not the only club following the youngster. Barcelona are reportedly seeking scouting reports ahead of January, while Benfica, Borussia Dortmund and Porto have also been linked with him.

Despite increasing interest from England and elsewhere in Europe, a move to prise Herrera away from La Bombonera in 2027 is unlikely to be straightforward.

Boca president Juan Roman Riquelme is determined to keep the heart of his trophy-winning squad together as the club prepare for next year's Copa Libertadores.

Head coach Rodolfo Arruabarrena has also told the board he wants the defender to stay, praising his strength in one-on-one duels and his willingness to learn from more experienced team-mates.

Boca have yet to receive a formal offer or begin transfer talks, putting the club in a strong position to resist early approaches while Herrera continues to develop in Buenos Aires.

A goalless draw with West Ham last weekend has proved to be Slegers’ final match in charge.

Slegers took charge as interim head coach in October 2024 and was then given the permanent job three months later.

That season ended in glory for Arsenal, who won their second Champions League title in May 2025. Earlier this year, the club won the inaugural FIFA Women’s Champions Cup.

However, results have dipped significantly this season and Arsenal have used the international break to make the change in head coach, with Slegers’ assistant Aaron D’Antino also leaving the club.

“It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renee, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here,” said director of women’s football Clare Wheatley.

“In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural FIFA Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron.

“After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary.”

Arsenal have won just three of their 11 matches in the WSL this season. Only two teams in the league have scored fewer goals.

A draw with Barcelona at the Nou Camp in the Women’s Champions League earlier this month was a positive result for Arsenal, who sit eighth of 18 teams in the competition.

Domestic results have not been good enough, though, and the search for a replacement will now begin.

“Renee is a wonderful person who has made a significant contribution to Arsenal, playing an integral role in some of the most historic achievements in the club’s history, including our Champions League and FIFA Champions Cup successes,” Arsenal CEO Richard Garlick said.

“Aaron also deserves special recognition for his service to Arsenal over many years, during which time he has helped us to win several titles.”

#1748. Arsenal, Liverpool and Man Utd 'told' they must pay £67m for teenager who stunned the Emirates

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 02:29, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 02:31

Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United are reportedly facing a fee of at least €80m (£67m) if they are to tempt teenage defender Joane Gadou away from Borussia Dortmund.

The 19-year-old French centre-back has made a swift breakthrough in Germany after joining from Red Bull Salzburg for €20m (£16.8m) last summer.

Dortmund believe they have found another exceptional prospect with the potential to make his mark on the international stage, and his estimated market value has reportedly already risen by 40% to €28m (£23.5m) according to Sport Witness.

The former Paris Saint-Germain academy player, recently linked with Liverpool, is under contract for the long term and has no release clause, leaving the Bundesliga club firmly in control of his future.

The leading Premier League clubs are likely to have stepped up their interest after Gadou delivered a commendable performance in Tuesday's 1-1 Champions League draw with Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

Viktor Gyokeres put the hosts ahead inside the opening 10 minutes, but Gadou supplied the match’s defining moment in the 55th minute, earning Dortmund a valuable point.

The teenager surged forward from his own half, fended off two Arsenal challenges and played a decisive pass for Maximilian Beier to equalise.

In his 89 minutes in North London, Gadou also made four clearances and completed 19 of his 22 passes, drawing warm praise from head coach Niko Kovac.

"We signed him because he is composed in possession and can contribute going forward," Kovac said. "He can break the lines and regularly create chances for the strikers. He is also very quick with the ball. It was a truly impressive performance.”

Bild via Sport Witness reports that Dortmund will not consider offers below four times the €20m (£16.8m)they paid Salzburg only months ago.

The club’s firm position is intended to discourage bids in January as Kovac's side aim to retain their key players for the second half of the 2026-27 campaign.

Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United are not the only clubs linked with the Frenchman: former side Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid are also reportedly interested.

#1747. Arsenal XI vs Man City: David Raya injury latest, predicted lineup, confirmed team news for Premier League

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal are set to make a late decision on the fitness of David Raya for Manchester City’s trip to north London on Sunday.

The goalkeeper missed Tuesday’s Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund due to a shoulder injury he picked up against Newcastle last weekend.

However, while there were fears that was a significant problem, scans have since showed that Raya avoided serious injury and his spell on the sidelines was not expected to be a lengthy one.

It remains to be seen whether Raya recovers in time to face City in the Premier League on Sunday, with Kepa Arrizabalaga ready to fill in again if required.

“I don’t know,” Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said of Raya’s availability at his pre-match press conference on Friday. “We still have a few hours before the game. We’re just trying to get everybody back.”

Asked whether there was hope that Raya would be available, Arteta added bluntly: “Yes.”

Ezri Konsa appears set to keep his place at centre-back alongside Gabriel, as Arsenal continue to cautiously manage William Saliba’s fitness.

Saliba was included in the matchday squad against both Newcastle and Dortmund but is yet to make a first-team appearance this season. It would be a surprise if he came straight in to face City.

It is expected that Riccardo Calafiori will return to the Arsenal starting lineup on Sunday after being rested in midweek, while Eberechi Eze could well get the nod in front of him on the left wing after impressing at St James’ Park.

Viktor Gyokeres scored against Dortmund but rival Kai Havertz is usually trusted in these biggest games by Arteta.

The German was given a full rest in that draw with Dortmund and he looks set to lead the line against City. Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi both remain out with thigh and hamstring injuries respectively.

#1745. Prediction: Deportivo La Coruna vs Barcelona

Barcelona will look to make it six consecutive victories in all competitions when they travel to Estadio Riazor on Sunday to face newly promoted Deportivo La Coruna in La Liga.

The Catalan giants sit comfortably at the top of the table and arrive in excellent form, while Deportivo continue their encouraging first season back in the top flight. Barcelona have won four of their last five meetings with Deportivo, including their famous 8-0 victory in the corresponding fixture during the 2015-16 campaign.

Deportivo have made a respectable return to La Liga after securing promotion by finishing second in last season’s Segunda Division.

Antonio Hidalgo’s side have collected three wins, six draws and four defeats from their opening 13 league matches, leaving them 12th in the standings with 15 points. While they suffered a disappointing 3-1 defeat away to Alaves last time out, their overall performances have been encouraging.

The Blue and Whites have picked up four points from their last three league matches and recorded an impressive 2-1 home victory over Osasuna in their most recent game at Riazor on November 2.

Home form has been solid, with nine points collected from six league fixtures. Deportivo will also take confidence from the fact that their most recent victory over Barcelona came on home soil, a 2-1 success in March 2017.

Historically, however, the head-to-head record heavily favours the visitors. The clubs have met 105 times, with Barcelona winning 63 matches compared to Deportivo’s 22, while 20 encounters have ended in draws.

Deportivo have relatively few injury concerns ahead of the fixture.

Bright Ede remains a major doubt because of a hamstring issue, while Zakaria Eddahchouri is struggling with a wrist problem and is also unlikely to be fully fit.

Up front, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang is expected to continue as the central striker. He has scored five La Liga goals this season, although he has not found the net in three matches since returning from a knee injury earlier this month.

Mariano Soriano and Luismi Cruz have both contributed two league goals this term and are expected to retain their places in the starting lineup.

Barcelona head to Galicia in outstanding form and with momentum continuing to build under Hansi Flick.

The Blaugrana arrive on the back of a 4-1 victory over Sabah in the Champions League, a result that left them fourth in the competition’s overall standings with 12 points. They are also in a commanding position domestically, sitting top of La Liga with 36 points from 13 matches.

Barcelona have won 12 of their first 13 league fixtures, suffering only one defeat, and currently hold a three-point advantage over Real Madrid and a five-point lead over Atletico Madrid. Their latest league outing produced a 3-2 victory over Villarreal.

The Catalan club have been the most prolific attacking side in Spain this season, scoring an extraordinary 51 goals in just 13 league fixtures. They now face a key sequence of matches against Deportivo, Atletico Madrid and Celta Vigo before resuming their Champions League campaign against Manchester City on December 8.

Barcelona are expected to receive a significant boost with the return of Lamine Yamal, who missed the Champions League victory over Sabah due to a minor ankle problem but is set to return to the starting lineup.

There will be no Fermin Lopez, however, after his red card against Villarreal. Roony Bardghji and Xavi Espart also remain unavailable because of knee and ankle injuries respectively.

There is more positive news elsewhere, with both Rodri and Andreas Christensen potentially available for selection. The ankle injury suffered by Alejandro Balde against Sabah is not considered serious, and he could also return to the squad.

Following the European fixture, Flick could restore several key players to the starting lineup, including Eric Garcia, Pau Cubarsi, Joao Cancelo, Dani Olmo and Raphinha.

Deportivo have adapted well to life back in La Liga and have shown they can be competitive at Riazor, but this represents one of their toughest tests of the season.

Barcelona arrive in exceptional form, boasting the league’s most potent attack and a squad that continues to grow in confidence under Flick. Deportivo may be capable of finding the net, particularly with Aubameyang leading the line, but the visitors possess too much quality across the pitch and should have enough to maintain their advantage at the top of the table.

#1744. The truth behind Manchester United triggering Bruno Fernandes contract extension

Manchester United had the January transfer window in mind when triggering Bruno Fernandes’ contract extension.

Standard Sport understands that Man Utd have activated their option to extend their captain’s deal by one year.

Fernandes’ current terms were due to expire at the end of the current season, but now run until the summer of 2028.

Fernandes confirmed last week that he had put contract negotiations with United on hold due to the club’s ongoing struggles on the pitch, having already rejected two offers of new terms.

Man Utd head into the Premier League weekend sitting in 19th place in the Premier League, and welcome sixth-placed Brentford to Old Trafford on Saturday in what is new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first home game in charge.

Fernandes has struggled to reproduce the form that earned him a host of individual awards last season, and Standard Sport understands that both parties believe it is sensible to return to negotiations at a later date.

But that left Fernandes open to approaches for foreign teams with pre-contract offers ahead of the summer.

To prevent any further distractions, Fernandes has been tied up for a further 12 months and will return to the negotiation table once the club are on more assured footing form-wise.

But an exit this summer can not yet be ruled out.

Fernandes may not be able to help his team-mates on Saturday, though, having been struck down by an illness which prevented him from training on Friday morning.

Confirming the issue later on Friday, Pochettino said of Fernandes: "He's affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and, today, he cannot be part of the training session.

"We'll see. We are going to see during the day and tomorrow, how he wakes up, and we'll see. We're not going to take any risks, because you know when this type of situation happens, you don't feel [you can]. We are going to pay attention but, still, we decide nothing."

#1743. Arsenal transfer news: Championship club prepare offer for Ethan Nwaneri, underused at Dortmund

By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 06:25

Ethan Nwaneri was the breakout star of Arsenal's 2024-25 season, but he has endured a difficult period for several months.

Short of game time at Arsenal, the 19-year-old Englishman was loaned to Marseille in the second half of last season. It was an underwhelming spell, during which the winger started only four times and was labelled a flop.

This season, Arsenal decided to send him out on loan again, this time to Borussia Dortmund.

However, the England Under-21 international no longer really features in the plans of Niko Kovac. Although he was used on many occasions at the start of the season, Nwaneri has not been in Dortmund's starting line-up since 17 October, away to Union Berlin (0-0).

Since that game, he has made a string of appearances in the final minutes of matches and has been left on the bench for the big games, against Bayern Munich (2-2) and Arsenal (1-1).

As a result, the player, who belongs to Arsenal, has played only 29 minutes in the German club's last seven outings, which is insufficient game time. This situation could also benefit West Ham United.

According to FootballTransfers, West Ham are preparing a loan offer to bring Nwaneri to the club in January.

The London club, 13th in the Championship, are looking to strengthen their squad in an attempt to return to the Premier League. However, the deal is far from straightforward, as Arsenal will first have to recall their youngster from Dortmund.

The British outlet points out that Nwaneri's loan at Borussia Dortmund does not include an option or obligation to buy. Arsenal have a recall clause which gives them the possibility of bringing their youngster back in January.

However, the Bundesliga leaders paid a loan fee, reportedly between £3.4m and £4.3m (€4m-€5m), and are covering the player's wages. Therefore, if Arsenal activate the recall clause for Nwaneri, they would have to reimburse the loan fee to Borussia Dortmund.

It therefore remains to be seen whether Arsenal will be prepared to give up that compensation to allow their talented youngster to join an environment more conducive to his progress, and whether the London club will demand another paid loan this winter.

West Ham are, in any case, lurking and ready to position themselves for the deal.

#1742. Manchester United XI vs Brentford: Bruno Fernandes latest, predicted lineup, confirmed team news for Premier League

Bruno Fernandes is a doubt for Manchester United as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to welcome Brentford to Old Trafford on Saturday.

The club captain was unable to train on Friday morning due to a virus, which has thrown into doubt his involvement in Pochettino’s first home match in charge.

Pochettino is still figuring out how best to set up his new team, and this is a potentially huge spanner to throw into the works.

Fernandes’s absence could see Matheus Cunha move into the No10 role, supported by Amad Diallo and Patrick Dorgu, with Bryan Mbeumo leading the line.

Elsewhere, the new manager also has a decision to make in defence. Having opted for a back three in the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield last weekend, Pochettino switched to a four-man defence for the chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting on Wednesday, in which Fernandes scored both goals.

Although Brentford will fancy their chances of victory based on the respective league positions of the two clubs - Man Utd 19th, the Bees in sixth - United will be urged by their fans to attack. As such, a more timid back three seems unlikely.

It will be a case of balancing fitness levels with only two days of rest between games. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens has come under fire in recent weeks for his performances, but back-up Karl Darlow has struggled with injury since arriving in the summer.

Pochettino’s defensive options are fairly limited. Leny Yoro is available after his early red card against Liverpool was overturned, while Harry Maguire was restored to the starting XI for the Sporting game.

Brentford’s pace in behind may necessitate a quicker backline, meaning Maguire could make way again here, having also reportedly complained of an injury after the midweek match.

Lisandro Martinez has been at left-back, but Dorgu’s attacking qualities will likely be required on Saturday and Luke Shaw is also now back in training. By moving Martinez back to centre-half alongside Yoro, Pochettino can find the pace required. Diogo Dalot may get the nod ahead of Noussair Mazraoui at right-back.

Should Fernandes be passed fit, the attack continues to pick itself - if not their exact positions.

Fernandes was deployed on the left behind Cunha in the defeat by Liverpool, while Mbeumo was briefly used as the lone forward under Michael Carrick.

Here, we’re predicting Cunha to lead the line after his midweek rest due to suspension, with Fernandes in behind as the No10 and Mbeumo on the left wing.

If Amad is fit enough to start after being forced off in the draw with Sporting, expect the Ivorian on the right flank. If not, youngster Shea Lacey could be a candidate to start.

Marcus Rashford and Benjamin Sesko remain injured, as do midfielders Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte. Pochettino revealed that Baleba would be out for 10 to 12 weeks from when he sustained his hamstring issue against Roma in early November.

By OLLIE LEWIS, SPORTS DIGITAL EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER

Published: 05:58 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:41 EST, 23 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino hauled his beleaguered Man United stars back into Carrington early on Monday morning after the new manager's chastening Anfield bow on Sunday.

Pochettino, who replaced Michael Carrick last week, was served a sobering reality check at the hands of United's fierce rivals Liverpool, with the Red Devils on the receiving end of a 4-0 trouncing on Merseyside.

The Argentine bemoaned the impact of what he described as a harsh red card against defender Leny Yoro in the opening eight minutes of the contest, but admitted he has plenty to do to turn things around - with United stuck in 19th in the Premier League table.

And Pochettino had his players check in for training early on Monday morning, with a downcast Bruno Fernandes and his team-mates spotted arriving at around 8.30am - roughly an hour earlier than under Carrick.

Under Carrick's stewardship, players were given the day after a game off, and it remains to be seen whether Pochettino will do away with that approach in favour of a recovery day at the club's training ground - a similar approach to that taken by former United boss Ruben Amorim.

Man United stars were ordered back into training on Monday after their trouncing at Anfield

Matthijs de Ligt cut a contemplative figure as he drove through the gates at Carrington

Director of football Jason Wilcox continues to have questions to answer after Man United were unable to elevate themselves out of the relegation zone

News also came on Monday that Man United are appealing to the FA over Yoro’s controversial red card.

Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute for a challenge on Alexander Isak on the edge of the penalty box. The Frenchman was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free kick as 10-man United were thrashed 4-0.

However, United insist that Yoro did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first.

The club have notified the FA of their intention to appeal in the hope of having Yoro’s one-match ban overturned so he can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

In September, Pro Ref boss Howard Webb apologised to United when Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand after VAR incorrectly ruled that teammate Enzo Fernandez was not interfering with play as he tried to head the ball in an offside position.

Last season, Webb acknowledged that the match officials got it wrong when they decided not to send off Brentford captain Nathan Collins for hauling back Bryan Mbeumo inside the box as United lost 3-1 at the Gtech Community Stadium.

New United head coach Pochettino blamed Yoro’s red card for the heavy defeat in his first game in charge, and was unhappy that Barrott took no action over a similar incident involving Jeremy Jacquet and Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty area moments earlier.

'So painful, so disappointed,' said the Argentine. 'It's not OK to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after eight minutes. Now we can explain everything, but the damage is done – it's so painful.

'It's clear that after eight minutes the plan was in the bin. Do you think that is easy? Even the best team in the world playing in this situation concedes four goals or maybe more.

'We are not going to lose more than one game how we lost today. I take the responsibility, and we keep pushing.

'We feel pain for this defeat, but we need to keep our heads up and translate that anger into energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game.

'We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing-room.

'The players are feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

'We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.'

But more critical were former Red Devils Roy Keane and Gary Neville, both of whom were pushed to extremes assessing the match after the final whistle.

Lisandro Martinez was among the Man United defenders that Gary Neville did not feel were up to the task at Anfield

But incoming manager Pochettino was keen to place the majority of blame on the harsh red card doled out to Leny Yoro

Neville was driven to slapping his face in the Sky Sports studio to demonstrate Man United's defenders' lack of hunger and poise.

'I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they've got something fixed in here', he said before pointing to his head.

'I never see any of them look like that,' he added. 'They look like that -'

Neville then stared into the middle distance for a few moments to share the blankness he sees on the faces of the back line, before spitting: 'Wake up!'

The Overlap broadcaster slapped himself a number of times while repeating 'wake up!' and adding: 'You play for Man United'.

Keane was pushed to the brink of swearing in his snap description of the team's performance, adding that he thought Neville's verdict - that the 4-0 scoreline might have been worse under the circumstances - took players off the hook.

'If I hear that one more time from the lads in the commentary that 4-0 is not too bad when you're down to 10 men - has a team ever got a result with 10 men before?' Keane said immediately after the final whistle. 'It can be done.

'I thought United were desperate. I thought they were so bad and everyone and Nev, who played for Man United saying 4-0 ain't bad.'

'(The red card) doesn't help but you're telling me they couldn't have done better? They lost 4-0 with 10 men, that's not too bad? Has a team ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality - I can't believe what I'm hearing from people.

'You played for the club, saying 4-0 isn't too bad. Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish. Liverpool were excellent, but how easy did United make it for them? I can't believe what I'm watching sometimes.

'This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers.

'When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making? Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying 4 is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'

#1740. Camarda recalls emotion of disallowed UCL goal and Gabbia’s words: “I burst into tears”

Francesco Camarda has spoken about his Champions League goal that never was today, and how it was an AC Milan dream come true.

Camarda first became known to Milan as a youngster, but he announced himself further when he became Serie A’s youngest-ever appearance maker. He almost then went to a European level, with a goal in the Champions League. However, it wasn’t to be.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

On his debut in the competition, the starlet bagged a goal which would’ve made him the Rossoneri’s youngest-ever scorer in Europe’s main stage. Yet it was ruled out for offside and a few years on, the now 18-year-old is still waiting for a first competitive goal for the Diavolo.

Speaking to Vice, the striker opened up about his dream of playing in the Champions League at San Siro, his emotions after his goal (and it later being disallowed) and how his teammates rallied around him, as MilanVibes relayed.

“As a child, I used to say to my dad: imagine if one day I could walk into San Siro and hear the Champions League anthem, accompanied by the roar of the entire stadium. When it actually happened, I thought back to that little boy and realised I had realised a dream.

“When I stepped onto the pitch, I had an incredible adrenaline rush. Then the goal came, and I felt the whole stadium explode. I also felt the affection of my teammates, who immediately raised me into the air.

“However, when I looked at the scoreboard and saw that the VAR check was in progress, I was already convinced the goal would be disallowed.

“When I returned home that evening, with my parents and cousin, I burst into tears. I was overjoyed by the goal, but at the same time deeply disappointed by what had happened. It wasn’t easy at first, but I also worked on my mental health and managed to put that moment behind me.

“Today, I’m proud of the journey I’ve taken and of having overcome those difficulties.”

“I remember what Gabbia told me: he was sorry for what happened, but he explained that the experience should give me even more motivation. It should push me to improve, to train harder, and to work so I can relive even more wonderful emotions.”

“In football, there are positive and negative opinions; it has always been this way and will continue to be this way. A player’s true strength lies in not being influenced by what is said, because, regardless of whether you do well or badly, someone will always find a reason to judge you.”

#1739. Tottenham: Roberto De Zerbi confirms new Dejan Kulusevski plan ahead of Sunderland trip

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Roberto De Zerbi has revealed that Dejan Kulusevski is closing in on his first Tottenham start in more than a year and a half.

Kulusevski made an emotional return to fitness last month, coming off the bench for his first appearance in 526 days following a serious patella injury as Spurs beat Coventry 3-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

The Swedish playmaker has since seen his minutes managed, with cameo appearances against Chelsea, Crystal Palace and Leeds before the international break.

Kulusevski was subsequently called up to Sweden’s squad for their Nations League fixtures against Bosnia and Poland earlier this month, playing a combined 54 minutes for Graham Potter’s side.

Spurs remain cautious about risking Kulusevski. But the 26-year-old’s performances over the international break have now convinced De Zerbi that he is nearly ready to start for the first time since Spurs’ 2-0 defeat to Crystal Palace on May 11, 2025.

“Listen, I am thinking to start maybe not now, but I think we are very close to start the game. He is working well. I watched his games in the national team just to understand the physical condition,” De Zerbi said in his pre-Sunderland press conference on Friday afternoon.

“He played the first game as a winger and the second game as a No.10 and especially in the second game he played very well, but we have to be good to understand the right moment to put him on the pitch. I think medical staff, physical staff, they are working very well with him and we can’t lose any time, but we can’t take any risk because he is a special player for us.”

Spurs have paid extra attention this season to managing the minutes of players with a history of injuries, with Dominic Solanke, Destiny Udogie and James Maddison all having faced spells out of the side in a bid to minimise the risk of them suffering long-term issues.

Udogie returned to the starting lineup for the first time since October’s 1-1 draw with Manchester United as Spurs beat Ipswich 2-0 last weekend.

Solanke, meanwhile, made just his sixth league start of the season, getting on the scoresheet in the second-half to seal the three points.

Asked about the pair, De Zerbi admitted that while they were making progress, Udogie would need to remain under close supervision from the club’s medical staff over the next three to four weeks.

“They’re working well also this week, both,” De Zerbi continued.

“Dominic Solanke, I think, played very well in the last game against Ipswich, and also Udogie.

“I think we have to manage Udogie better than Solanke because Udogie needs to stay with the medical staff, focusing on him for another three, four weeks, and then if he goes over this four weeks, I think for him it’s not a problem.”

#1738. Is Goalscoring a Problem for Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal?

Probably the strangest thing about the debate over Arsenal’s attacking power is that it exists at all.

On the surface, the Premier League champions appear to be moving in the right direction. Their football is more fluid than it was a year ago, their positional rotations are more ambitious and they have become less dependent on set-pieces as a source of goals. Yet as Manchester City arrive at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday, there is a growing sense that Arsenal’s attack remains their one area of vulnerability.

That feeling is not driven solely by statistics. It is driven by matches. Arsenal continue to control games, create pressure and dominate territory, but too often they fail to establish the kind of leads that allow them to relax. The result is a team that wins regularly but leaves itself with very little margin for error.

The arrival of Viktor Gyokeres in 2025 was supposed to address a long-standing concern. Arsenal wanted a recognized centre-forward capable of turning dominance into goals and relieving some of the burden on the rest of the team.

His record has not been poor. Fourteen goals last season made him Arsenal’s leading scorer, but there has remained a sense that the club are still looking for another level in attack. That explains why they explored ambitious moves for players such as Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez during the summer.

Those pursuits revealed something important about Arsenal’s thinking. Arteta is no longer looking for squad depth or developmental prospects. He wants a world-class attacker capable of deciding the biggest matches and carrying the attack through difficult periods.

The difficulty is that such players are rarely available, particularly in January.

Arteta has spent much of the past year trying to make the team less predictable. Defenders now appear in advanced positions. Midfielders rotate into wide areas. Attackers exchange roles with greater frequency than before. The movement has become more dynamic and considerably harder to defend against.

That evolution can be seen throughout the side. Piero Hincapie and Riccardo Calafiori frequently appear in positions normally reserved for attackers. Full-backs move into central areas. Wingers drift inside. Arsenal’s attacking patterns are far less rigid than they were during previous seasons.

The trade-off is that this style demands excellent decision-making in the final third. When those decisions are slightly off, Arsenal can dominate possession and territory without fully translating that superiority into goals.

That has happened often enough this season to become a concern.

No team loses a player of Bukayo Saka’s quality without consequences.

For years, Arsenal’s attack has benefited from having a player capable of creating and finishing chances at elite levels. His injury has inevitably reduced the threat they carry, particularly in moments when matches require individual inspiration.

The larger concern is that several attacking players have not fully compensated for his absence. There have been signs of improvement from Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze, while Kai Havertz continues to deliver goals in important matches. Yet none of them has consistently provided the level of output that allows Arsenal to overwhelm opponents.

That is why so many of their victories remain narrow despite long periods of superiority.

Arsenal trust their defence enough to protect one-goal leads, and that confidence is understandable given their recent record. Yet continually operating with such small margins creates risks – the picture at the top of the Premier League table would’ve been far more interesting at this point had Liverpool been given the penalty that should’ve been awarded for Jurrien Timber’s shirt-pull on Alexander Isak, for example.

The timing of this discussion is significant. Manchester City visit this weekend. Trips to Brentford and Tottenham follow shortly afterwards. Then comes a Champions League meeting with Real Madrid. These are precisely the fixtures in which elite attacking players justify their reputations.

Arteta has spoken optimistically about the chances his team continue to create, arguing that improved efficiency will naturally follow if the Gunners maintain their current level of performance. There is logic to that view. Teams that consistently generate opportunities tend to score eventually.

The question is whether Arsenal can afford to wait.

Because while their football has evolved positively, they are still encountering the same issue that has lingered around the club for several seasons. When matches become tight and opportunities are limited, there remains a feeling that Arsenal do not possess quite enough goals across the squad.

Few managers have transformed a club more successfully than Arteta. He has rebuilt Arsenal’s culture, restored their competitiveness and ultimately delivered the Premier League title. His latest tactical evolution has made the team more flexible and more entertaining to watch.

Yet the challenge facing him now may be the most difficult one of all.

The gap between a very good attack and a truly great one is often filled by players who are almost impossible to sign. Arsenal appear to have reached the point where collective improvements alone may not be enough. The structure is strong, the football is intelligent and the squad is packed with quality.

What they may still need is the sort of forward capable of turning twenty good minutes into a three-goal lead.

Until they find that player, questions about Arsenal’s firepower are unlikely to disappear entirely, irrespective of their lead in the Premier League title race. The encouraging aspect for Arteta is that they remain champions despite those concerns. The worrying aspect is that the teams chasing them know exactly where the vulnerability lies.

#1737. Barcelona transfer news: Summer signing set for loan exit this winter

By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 06:37

During the last summer transfer window, Barcelona signed high-calibre players such as Rodri and Anthony Gordon to improve Hansi Flick's squad immediately, but also invested in two young players: Hamza Abdelkarim and Jesse Bisiwu.

The 18-year-old Belgian winger joined the Catalan club from Belgium's Club NXT for £7.2m (€8.5m).

A significant investment by the Catalan club. As expected, the Leuven native is not yet ready to play at the highest level. As a result, he has still not played under Flick.

With Lamine Yamal absent, Bisiwu was expected to make his first appearance in the Champions League against Sabah (1-4) on Wednesday. Although he was on the substitutes' bench, he did not come on.

For the time being, he has to settle for appearances with Barca Atletic. The Belgian gem has played eight games with the Catalan reserve team and provided one assist. However, this usage does not seem to satisfy Barcelona's hierarchy.

Indeed, according to information from Walfoot, Barcelona are considering loaning the 18-year-old in January to allow him to gain game time in a good-quality professional league. According to the Belgian outlet, three destinations are already emerging to host the Belgian prospect.

They include Ajax, where Jordi Cruyff holds an executive role and could ease talks, as well as Rangers. Both clubs are reportedly interested in the young left winger, as is 'a renowned Ligue 1 club', whose identity has not been revealed.

#1736. Man City XI vs Arsenal: Predicted lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest for Premier League

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Manchester City head to Arsenal this weekend in desperate need of a morale-boosting victory.

Enzo Maresca’s side have picked up just one point from the last 12 available in the Premier League, with a disappointing home draw with Fulham following successive defeats at the hands of Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest.

Sitting third and already six points behind leaders Arsenal after only 11 games, many pundits predict that City’s title chances will effectively be over if they lose again in north London on Sunday.

City are also still waiting for their appeal to be heard against the guilty verdict returned by an independent panel back in September on their charges of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules across a nine-season period between 2009/10 and 2017/18. They deny any wrongdoing.

Maresca has to find the right team to beat an Arsenal side that have lost just twice at home across all competitions in 2026.

Gianluigi Donnarumma will start in goal as usual, with the back four in front of him likely consisting of Matheus Nunes, Ruben Dias, Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol.

Dias was rested for the home draw with Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday night, with the City captain set to be restored to the starting XI here.

Nico O’Reilly has emerged as the first-choice option at left-back in recent weeks, but the defensive ability of Gvardiol could be key in a potentially cagey match.

Maresca has experimented with the construction of his midfield in the last few games. Enzo Fernandez was deployed as a No10 against Napoli, but a return to the preferred paring of the Argentine and Elliot Anderson at the base of City’s midfield feels likely at Arsenal.

Similarly, Iliman Ndiaye has impressed on the right wing in recent weeks. Rayan Cherki was deployed out wide against Napoli, but has been most effective as a No10.

Jeremy Doku has become trusted on the left, while Erling Haaland cannot be left out - even if he is enduring a goalscoring drought by his usual lofty standards.

Maresca revealed at his pre-match press conference on Friday that Antoine Semenyo was close to returning from a knee injury sustained against Ipswich last month, though the trip to Arsenal will come too soon for his comeback.

#1735. Montella describes ‘dream’ Milan opportunity, Berlusconi and the Supercoppa: “An incredible feeling”

Vincenzo Montella’s time with AC Milan was ‘a dream’ for him, but he failed to achieve much during his time at the helm.

Looking back on Montella’s time leading Milan is tricky. On paper, the Italian had a strong tenure at the club, achieving a 50% win rate and only losing 18 of his 64 games in charge at San Siro, not a terrible record by any means.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He even ended a five-year trophy drought with a win against Juventus in the Supercoppa Italiana and returned the Rossoneri to Europe, with a sixth-place finish in the 2016/17 season. In itself, that was a first since 2014.

This is where context matters, though. The start of the 2017/18 season was tough, as the Diavolo won six of their first 14 games and he was sacked before December. Despite that, he still views the club in an excellent light.

Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport’s ‘La Tripletta’ podcast, Montella went over his time with the club and how he fulfilled a dream by taking the job, as MilanPress relays.

“It was a fantastic experience there [at Milan] too, it was my dream. Then, as a professional, it’s a little different, but when I was thirteen I was a fan of that AC Milan team. My older brother took me to see Maradona’s Napoli team twice to make me a Napoli fan, and Maradona scored three goals.

“Despite this, my idol was Van Basten because I was a striker: I studied him and dreamed of becoming like him, and so I was a Milan fan. I knew everything about Milan, so for me it was an incredible feeling to join Milan.”

“He liked to talk about football; he liked to give advice even when it was a bit out of context at the time, because he always had the mentality of having Van Basten as a centre forward with Papin, a two-time Ballon d’Or winner, on the bench. He wanted me to play with two strikers, and I tried to plug the gap for months.

“I told him it was difficult; I knew all the lineups of those years. I was a Milan fan: the starter was Van Basten and the reserve was Papin, both Ballon d’Or winners. So, ‘If you buy me some players like that, rest assured that I’ll play them both.'”

“It was a year when we returned to Europe. I think it had been two or three years since Milan had been there, and it was something new at the time. We won a trophy, a small one. Just the other night I saw Galliani at a dinner; he reminded me of it and remembers it perfectly.

“I have to say that I found him to be the perfect manager at the time, because he was always on my side when it came to pressure; he gave me complete autonomy in my decisions and he helped me with everything, from the number of collaborators to new things; whatever I asked for, he was always on the coach’s side.

“And so for me he was truly an incredible manager, who in that phase, in that change, was fundamental even in achieving these small results, especially after Berlusconi’s great AC Milan.

“We deserved to win even in regulation time: we had some easy chances to win it, then it came to penalties. Gigio saved the penalty from Dybala, who kicked it really hard, but he filled the net with it.”

“I was a little worried from the beginning because there was this obsession with publicising everything, almost like a publicity stunt, so I was a little worried. In theory, there was sharing, at least that’s what it looked like, but I couldn’t back out when in reality that wasn’t always the case.

“And so sometimes there were players I hadn’t even consulted about, who would arrive and then say, ‘It was shared,’ and when you’re there, you can’t say otherwise. Certainly, when you build a team and have the budget, the first thing you do is: we had a goalkeeper, I’ll get a centre forward, we were missing a centre forward.

“In the final selection, the centre forward was the only one left, with a budget of 15-20 million. And then Kalinic… yes, I chose him because that was the final budget. So our, let’s say, second-choice striker was paid thirty-eight million, if I remember correctly, who was André Silva, and the first striker was paid half that.

“And so, in my opinion, a misunderstanding of this kind was created, with so many changes, even though at that stage we weren’t even playing badly for having fifteen new players.

“We still had Calhanoglu, who wasn’t feeling well, coming off months of suspension. The team was still being built: we weren’t in line with the Scudetto objectives that had been announced, but certainly, given our development, we were absolutely on target.

“Who would I have signed up front? At the time, we were probably negotiating for Aubameyang, if I remember correctly. Ronaldo? No, I didn’t believe it, not at all.”

#1734. Ian Holloway SACKED by Swindon two days after trying to confront angry fans in feisty full-time scenes at Newport - with Premier League cult hero claiming club's training ground is haunted

Published: 05:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:57 EST, 23 November 2026

Ian Holloway has been sacked by Swindon just two days after attempting to confront angry fans following defeat to Newport on Saturday.

The journeyman manager had himself called the 2-0 loss on the road 'unforgivable' after he was taunted by home supporters chanting that he would be 'sacked in the morning' after the result.

Holloway had intended to go down the tunnel after the final whistle, and passed the away stand on his route out, taking off his cap as he held up his hands in resignation.

But as boos rained down on him, the 63-year-old could not resist the urge to engage, looking to answer back to the fans before he was restrained by security.

Last month, Holloway described himself as a 'dead man walking' with the Robins mired 17th in League Two, but Monday morning saw him despatched after two seasons in charge.

'Since joining the club towards the end of 2024, Ian has played an important role in stabilising our on-field position and helping the club make progress season upon season,' the Swindon statement announcing his departure read.

Saturdays eh.#STFC pic.twitter.com/1GL3blApwW

Ian Holloway was caught up in a clash with fans after Swindon's defeat to Newport County - shortly before he was sacked (Source: X/Loathed Stranger)

The journeyman manager oversaw two seasons at the club, saving them from relegation in 2024-25

'However, following careful consideration of recent results and performances, the club believes that now is the right time to take a different direction.

'This has not been an easy decision, but the board firmly believes that it is important to make difficult decisions when necessary, always with the best interests of Swindon Town at heart.'

Holloway cut a disillusioned figure at Rodney Parade as he gave a heartfelt assessment of his side's performance after defeat to the Exiles.

'It's devastating,' said Holloway. 'I'm bitterly disappointed. Did I expect my team to do that? Not in a million years.

'We're getting regular mistakes from almost everyone in that backline and in that midfield. We knew what type of game it was going to be. There's no excuses. I've just said to them "what on Earth do you think you're doing?" To start that way? It was so passive it was unforgivable.

'It's very painful at the minute. It'll come back at the manager in the end if I listen to all these people (from the stands).

'This is football. I've been in it a long time. This is my life.'

Holloway also questioned the desire of his players, continuing: 'Bitterly disappointed in all of them and disappointed for the fans. I get it, that didn't look like our team.

'They scored two ugly goals. All our chances that we had, normally we take them.

'Where's the fight? It's a local derby. I'm sorry, they've done their bits better than us.'

Holloway has endured an uneven stint at Swindon since 2024, saving the club from relegation in his first season but failing to challenge for the promotion places as time wore on.

Memorably, the former Crystal Palace and Queen's Park Rangers manager claimed that the training ground was haunted shortly after his arrival in Wiltshire.

Holloway had first suggested that there had been 'some strange things happening' after the club captain Ollie Clarke had ruptured his ankle in training, before enlisting his wife Kim to free spirits potentially trapped in the South West.

'I'm absolutely devastated so I'm going to try and cleanse the training ground area because people are telling me it's haunted,' Holloway said on BBC Radio Wiltshire in November 2024.

'There's a graveyard somewhere near. Honestly, I'm not joking.

'I think our training ground is very close to an ancient burial site so I'm going to get my wife to come up and say sorry to all these people and hopefully we'll have a bit more luck.'

#1733. 'Weighed a little on the team', former Lyon team-mate gives Rayan Cherki verdict

By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 06:53

Rayan Cherki made a strong impression on Jeffinho during their time together at Olympique Lyonnais in 2023. Appearing as a guest on the Charla Podcast, the Brazilian forward first praised the technical qualities of the current Manchester City player, before describing a much more divisive character.

'Rayan Cherki. What a player! He is a bit annoying, but he strikes the ball and drives it with both feet. He is very strong' - he explained.

Jeffinho then went on to explain what could bother him about the Frenchman. 'You can see it in the way he plays. He dribbles and looks at the others' - the Brazilian said, naming Bradley Barcola among the best players he has played alongside and liked.

The testimony becomes even more interesting when he discusses relationships within the Lyon dressing room.

According to Jeffinho, Cherki belonged to a fairly closed group that also included Corentin Tolisso, Alexandre Lacazette and Anthony Lopes. The Brazilian describes a 'small clique' of important players who stayed together a lot and, in his view, had real influence in the team.

At the time, Lyon's management had nevertheless denied the existence of a 'Lyonnais gang'.

Asked about the player with the most assertive temperament in this circle, Jeffinho naturally named Cherki.

He explained that the group 'weighed a little on the team', while not hiding that their attitude could sometimes annoy him. His testimony remains nuanced, however: with each criticism of the Frenchman's behaviour, the former Lyon player returns to his immense quality as a player.

Jeffinho also extended his judgement to Cherki's current situation at Manchester City. 'Cherki plays extremely well, but you also have to respect the others' - he said, before suggesting that his attitude could sometimes have a negative impact on his team.

A very personal view of the attacking midfielder, but one that above all sheds light on the relationships he observed in the Lyon dressing room.

Their two statement signings from last summer - Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak - are both hitting top form, which bodes well for this weekend’s derby showdown.

Dominik Szoboszlai seems to have put his injury woes in the past, and while young Trey Nyoni has impressed when given opportunities this term, Alexis Mac Allister will surely get the nod alongside him in the midfield engine room as Ryan Gravenberch remains a doubt with ongoing heel pain.
