#1729. How Amorim picked apart Alvini’s gung-ho approach: Tactical analysis of AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone

AC Milan put on arguably their best display of the Ruben Amorim era so far as they beat Frosinone 5-1 at San Siro on Sunday.

Gabriele Calvani’s early own-goal kicked off what would be a miserable night for the Canarini, before Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. Patrizio Masini’s goal halved the deficit, and kept the game open going into the second half.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

From there, though, the Rossoneri ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both scored within minutes of coming off the bench, finishing counter-attacks, then Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It was a win that Milan needed to move back into the top four, also given that only Inter out of the top six sides in the table dropped points. Rohit Rajeev has the tactical breakdown from the win.

Ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Milan once again deployed a modified version of their 3-4-2-1, with Bartesaghi operating on the left. Alvini, meanwhile, had to cope without his striker Raimondo and opted for a 3-5-2, pairing Ghedjemis and Kvernadze up front.

Frosinone made their intentions clear from the opening seconds. Goalkeeper Palmisani immediately played a direct ball into a targeted zone, with Frosinone committing several players towards the expected landing area to create a numerical advantage and win the aerial duel.

Milan built from deep with three players at the back, while Maignan pushed forward to act as an additional centre-back. This created a 4v3 in the first line of build-up, forcing Frosinone’s front three of Ghedjemis, Kvernadze and Schmid to press deeper.

Their movement opened up space between Frosinone’s first and second pressing lines for Milan’s players to receive.

Milan built from deep with three players at the back, while Maignan pushed forward to act as an additional centre-back. This created a 4v3 in the first line of build-up, forcing Frosinone’s front three of Ghedjemis, Kvernadze and Schmid to press deeper. Their movement opened up space between Frosinone’s first and second pressing lines for Milan’s players to receive. However, it was Rabiot’s movement that proved decisive in creating the overload for Milan’s opening goal. With Frosinone committing three forwards to the press and keeping two players wide, only two midfielders and three defenders remained to deal with Milan’s build-up. Although Musah and Rabiot were initially marked, Rabiot dropped deeper into midfield to create a numerical advantage and free himself to receive possession.

— Rohit Rajeev (@keralista) November 23, 2026

However, it was Rabiot’s movement that proved decisive in creating the overload for Milan’s opening goal. With Frosinone committing three forwards to the press and keeping two players wide, only two midfielders and three defenders remained to deal with Milan’s build-up.

Although Musah and Rabiot were initially marked, Rabiot dropped deeper into midfield to create a numerical advantage and free himself to receive possession.

This movement directly contributed to Milan’s opening goal. Rabiot dropped between the lines to receive possession, forcing Cittadini to step out of his defensive position and follow him.

Rabiot then laid the ball off to Modric, who immediately played it into the space vacated by Cittadini. Under pressure, Frosinone inadvertently turned the ball into their own net to give Milan a 1-0 lead.

Frosinone looked to commit numbers into Milan’s half, creating ball-sided overloads to progress through the pitch. Their two wingers maintained wide positions to stretch Milan’s wing-backs and create more space in the central areas.

Out of possession, Frosinone adopted a 3-4-3 to match Milan’s 3-4-2-1 in possession. They also maintained a very high defensive line, looking to press Milan aggressively and win the ball back as high up the pitch as possible.

Milan allowed Frosinone to dictate possession, dropping into a deeper defensive block to invite them into their half. Once Frosinone advanced, Milan looked to win the ball back and launch quick counter-attacks.

Frosinone’s lack of a clear attacking structure and, more importantly, an organised rest defence left them vulnerable in transition. Milan exploited this disorganisation repeatedly, with the next four goals all benefiting from the spaces Frosinone left behind.

The second goal perfectly illustrated Milan’s approach in transition. Frosinone had committed ten players into Milan’s half, leaving very little defensive cover behind.

Ramos won possession, and Musah immediately played a vertical pass to release Moreira through on goal. Moreira and Rabiot then drew three recovering defenders towards them before creating the space for Ramos to finish.

Frosinone’s high-risk approach briefly paid off with Masini’s goal. They drew Milan into central areas before pressing aggressively to recover possession. With their players positioned close together, they were able to combine quickly and progress the ball towards Kvernadze.

A deflection off De Winter then took the ball into Ghedjemis’ path, allowing him to set up Masini for the finish.

Frosinone consistently targeted Milan’s left flank, particularly the space around Bartesaghi. The individual duel between Ghedjemis and Bartesaghi became a key feature of the game.

Ghedjemis repeatedly beat his marker in 1v1 situations and posed a threat. Recognising the problem, Amorim took Bartesaghi off at half-time.

After the break, Jashari and Pulisic began making coordinated counter-movements. Pulisic dropped deeper, drawing his marker away and creating space in the wide attacking area, which Jashari then exploited with an advancing run.

The goal was very similar to the movement Jashari made against Venezia, highlighting a recurring pattern in Milan’s attacking play.

Both Cisse’s and Pulisic’s goals came from a counter-attack following a Frosinone corner, for which they did not leave many men back.

For Cisse’s finish, his body orientation suggested he was going to shoot towards the goalkeeper’s right, prompting the keeper to adjust his stance accordingly. Cisse then went the other way, finding the opposite corner.

⚽️ GOAL ALPHADJO CISSE! 🔥 https://t.co/aMIgE9PXHc

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026

Pulisic, meanwhile, used the bridge of his foot to execute a delicate chip, lifting the ball over the advancing goalkeeper and completing the counter-attack.

⚽️ GOAL CHRISTIAN PULISIC 🇺🇸 https://t.co/B4mP55RJ8u

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026

We wrote something during the break about how Milan are over-performing relative to certain metrics. Above all, their actual goals scored was/is well above their Expected Goals, helped by the fact four players are converting an abnormally high percentage of chances.

With this in mind, the stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals, so they again out-performed what they created. And yet, the Rossoneri racked up five big chances which matches the number of goals scored.

So, perhaps everything can be taken with a pinch of whatever type of salt fits your narrative. Many would argue that Milan could have scored more given their brilliant on Sunday, yet xG would have you believe it was a ‘lucky’ margin in a game that should have been 2/3-1.

The visitors also racked up nine corners, the most Milan have conceded all season, but thankfully Amorim’s side managed to deal with them all relatively well.

#1728. Man City ‘close’ to major injury boost as Enzo Maresca reveals latest team news before Arsenal

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Antoine Semenyo is close to returning for Manchester City, Enzo Maresca has confirmed.

The Ghana international has not featured for Man City since sustaining a knee injury in the 3-2 victory over Ipswich on October 17, missing the last eight games across all competitions as a result.

During this period, City have not won a Premier League game and head to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday to face leaders and reigning champions Arsenal.

Semenyo is not expected to be available for the trip to north London, though he could return against either Leeds or Brentford within the next week following a positive update from Maresca.

“We have good news, Antoine is quite close,” Maresca said in Friday’s pre-match press conference. “It’s good news for us. He is already on the pitch - he is very close, hopefully it can be next week, we hope so.

“I was laughing with him yesterday or two days ago. I told him in the Premier League the last game we won was with him on the pitch, so I said we need him back soon to win games.

“Antoine is an important player but we have more players in his position that are doing well like Iliman in this moment. But he needs time to recover.”

Semenyo had been enjoying a decent start to his first full season as a Man City player before being struck down by injury, scoring twice and weighing in with three assists in seven appearances.

The winger also started City’s big away wins over Manchester United and Liverpool, two results that has boosted Maresca’s belief that his side can end their recent slump with victory at Arsenal.

He added: “I think we already showed this season we are able to win important games, to win away. So I don’t see any reason why we are not able to win there.

“We have shown this season we can win important games away. Old Trafford and Anfield are two important away games and Sunday we have another one.

“We showed already and we can win again.”

#1727. Andoni Iraola handed Liverpool boost ahead of Merseyside derby after 'severe' injury scare

By Lewis Blain | 27 Nov 2026 07:15

Liverpool have received encouraging news regarding Víctor Munoz after the winger suffered a worrying knee injury against Club Brugge on Wednesday evening.

The Spanish winger was forced off following a heavy collision during the first half of the 3-0 win, with the initial images raising fears of a potentially serious problem.

However, early tests have reportedly suggested that the injury is not as bad as first feared, offering Reds boss Andoni Iraola some welcome relief ahead of the Merseyside Derby on Sunday afternoon.

Munoz suffered the injury after his knee became caught during a strong collision with a Brugge player inside the opposition penalty area.

The incident prompted immediate concern among his teammates, with a stretcher brought onto the pitch to assist the winger. However, he eventually managed to leave the field under his own steam, accompanied by Dominik Szoboszlai.

It initially appeared particularly concerning, but subsequent tests have provided a more positive indication of the extent of the damage.

According to reports from Spain, the initial assessment suggests that Munoz has suffered a 'severe' blow to his knee rather than a serious injury. Definitive confirmation is still pending, but the early indications are encouraging.

Iraola also offered a cautiously optimistic assessment after the match.

"He felt a lot of pain at the moment, but by the end of the match he was feeling better. I hope it's nothing important," the Liverpool coach said.

Although it remains unclear whether Munoz will be fit for this weekend's Merseyside derby, the initial diagnosis is certainly reassuring for Iraola.

The severity of the collision and the sight of the stretcher initially suggested that Liverpool could be facing a significant injury setback, potentially ruling the winger out for an extended period.

Instead, the early tests indicate that the problem may be limited to a heavy blow, although the club will understandably wait for definitive confirmation before making any decisions on his availability.

With a major fixture approaching, Muñoz's potential involvement would be a welcome boost, but avoiding a serious injury is the most important outcome at this stage.

#1726. Bayern Munich slammed as 'despicable' and accused of 'co-ordinated' plot to undermine Jamal Musiala after club chief questioned star's contract due to his health issues - with Jude Bellingham, Michael Olise and Rio Ferdinand backing the youngster

Published: 10:38 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 11:29 EST, 23 November 2026

Bayern Munich have come under criticism from FIFA's players' union and leading figures in the game amid accusations that the club is attempting to slash Jamal Musiala's wages following his diagnosis with a 'neurological dysfunction'.

The Germany international was diagnosed over the summer with absence seizures, a form of epilepsy which causes 'brief but easily treatable seizures'.

Musiala shocked the sporting world when he collapsed in two matches earlier this season, with Bayern manager Vincent Kompany explaining that the player had suffered from a reaction to a change in his medication.

Comments from members of Bayern's hierarchy have sparked controversy in Germany and abroad, with senior figures appearing to question the length of the player's contract – which runs until 2030 – should Musiala not recover his form.

Honorary president Uli Hoeness was the first to speak out on the potential drop-off in form Musiala might suffer with long-term absences, claiming earlier this month that he 'may never regain the performance level he once had'.

'We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,' Hoeness told German outlet BR24.

Fifpro and international footballers have come out in support of Musiala over concerns that Bayern Munich might reduce his salary

Both Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have made comments suggesting consequences should Musiala not return to his level

Jan-Christian Dreesen also suggested that the club would need to 'assess' the situation if his performances do not return to their high heights

Chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen then backed up Hoeness's comments and implied that Musiala's contract may need to be 'assessed'.

'We're monitoring his level of play. He'll certainly need time to improve further – like any injured player,' Dreesen said in discussion with AZ. 'And then we need to calmly assess the situation and, if necessary, sit down with his family and management.

'Either we'll all be happy together and he'll be the same Jamal he always was – or, if he's a different Jamal along the way, we'll have to discuss it.'

'If we're not consistently at a level that also aligns with the economic realities, then we'll have to talk to each other. Nevertheless, we have a valid contract, and that's the end of it.'

The 23-year-old is one of Bayern's highest-earners, having signed a deal with the club to extend his time in Bavaria in February 2025. The deal is thought to be worth £18.4million per year.

Adding fuel to the fire days later was former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who told Sky Sports/RTL that he thought it was almost reasonable to discuss a renegotiation should Musiala not return to the level at which he once played.

'That is certainly possible and cannot be ruled out,' he said. 'Unfortunately, what we know suggests that it will be difficult to reach the level that he has so often shown here in this stadium.'

'We need to talk to the family, the player, and above all, the agency. Because then these sums are – sorry, with all due respect – no longer feasible.

'I can't imagine Jamal leaving the club or another club buying him under these circumstances. That's a problem. I think we handled this very sensitively with the player, and we're all interested in him coming back - ideally in top form. But what happens if that's not the case? Then we'll still have to think about the finances. And that's a task that the board and the supervisory board unfortunately have to make.'

Rummenigge added that he did not think it was 'problematic' for these discussions to be happening publicly, due to the club's interest in 'him coming back and playing well'.

But the player union Fifpro were forthright in their disagreement with his statements,  releasing a statement claiming that all parties currently sharing their views on Musiala's contract 'should know better'.

'Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession,' the statement read.

'In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.'

When this statement was shared to social media via journalist Fabrizio Romano, global talents including Jude Bellingham and Musiala's team-mate Michael Olise were among those to like the post.

Musiala collapsed on the pitch at two consecutive games in August (pictured being helped by team-mates against RB Leipzig)

The 23-year-old has been diagnosed with absence seizures and is managing his medication

Vincent Kompany has been supportive of his player's struggles, and took him off the bench with some success last weekend

Rio Ferdinand elaborated on those comments in a more detailed post on social media, adding that he believed the club are 'better than this'.

'If they want to negotiate more reasonable terms for the club going forward due to the health issues Jamal has, then surely speak to him and his team rather than to the media,' Ferdinand wrote on X. 'This situation must be hard enough to deal with for Jamal without the media and club officials talking about it publicly.

'Bayern Munich are one of the clubs who from afar have always carried themselves with a class and standard that most have admired. Sadly, this just doesn't feel like Bayern Munich in this situation.'

Criticisms were even more fiery in Germany, with the vice president of Germany's player union Michael Franz accusing the club of harassment.

'What the Bayern Munich officials are doing, and I don't mean Kompany and (Max) Eberl (director of sport), who have behaved impeccably, seems despicable to me,' Franz shared in an interview with Sport1. 'There is even something about it that resembles harassment.'

'A footballer's level of performance can be discussed publicly, but it is not right to talk about his illness and the salary he receives in such circumstances. We must not forget that Jamal Musiala has done everything in his power to come back.'

'Money has become more important than the person, and that is unacceptable.'

Former Bayern captain Stefan Effenberg stressed how important 'support and protection' from the club towards their players is, particularly for those in greater need like Musiala.

'We are talking about someone who is suffering from an illness. What I would have expected is for the club's senior officials to apologise,' Effenberg said, adding that he thought that the communications from the club had been 'disastrous'.

Musiala collapsed twice within four days in mid-August, first during Bayern's match against Leipzig – shortly after scoring – and then against Heidenheim.

He then returned to the pitch in September, netting against Bodo/Glimt in Champions League action and Union Berlin shortly before the first international break.

After suffering a hamstring injury, Musiala then spent time away from the side before his return at the end of last week – a match which also saw Harry Kane suffer an ankle injury which will keep him out for over three months.

Fifpro's statement went on to add that Bayern must be careful with their player's mental wellbeing as well as his physical issues.

'Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala,' the statement continued. 'Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.

'Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

'Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.'

Manchester United have reportedly activated their option to extend Bruno Fernandes’ contract.

But United always possessed the option to trigger an automatic one-year extension, which they have now done.

Paz joined Como in 2024 from Real Madrid in a deal worth around £5million, and it had long been expected that the player would return to the Spanish giants, who hold an €80m (£67m) buy-back clause for Paz.

But The Athletic report that Paz does not currently favour a return to Spain, where he will not be a key player, and is said to be attracted by the prospect of joining Man Utd who need a long-term replacement for captain Bruno Fernandes.

The race for Paz is set to be fierce, but Man Utd will hope they have an advantage over rivals in the form of new manager Mauricio Pochettino.

“That (a loan) was their idea, but it was never an option from my side,” Vuskovic said in an interview with the Times. “Because already I have been on three loans and for me, my family, my girlfriend, it’s too much to move, with all the languages, and it gets too much for the person, you know?

Los Blancos have a buy-back option for Paz next summer said to be valued at around €80m, though he is also attracting plenty of interest from elsewhere.

CaughtOffside cite reports claiming that Arsenal are closely tracking the 22-year-old, along with Liverpool and Tottenham, with a return to Madrid looking unlikely as things stand.

Richarlison is open to moving to Saudi Arabia to end his Tottenham exile.

The striker has been frozen out at Spurs by manager Roberto De Zerbi after failing to agree a summer exit.

Everton, Vasco da Gama and Trabzonspor were all said to have explored deals for Richarlison, who ended up staying put at Spurs despite being left out of De Zerbi's Premier League squad.

Manchester United fans will be dismayed by reports that Mauricio Pochettino will have just £50million to improve his squad during the January transfer window.

A leaky defence has led to calls from ex-players such as Gary Neville for significant investment, but it appears Man Utd will try to do their business on a tight budget in January.

The second window of the season often leads to inflated prices, with clubs capitalising upon other teams’ struggles and desperate need for new players.

#1723. Iraola: Liverpool improvement not only down to Wirtz and Isak

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Andoni Iraola insisted Liverpool's recent turnaround in form was "not about Florian Wirtz or Alexander Isak".

The Reds have won each of their last three games in all competitions, following up a 4-0 win over Manchester United in the Premier League with a 3-0 Champions League victory at Club Brugge.

Isak scored twice in the win against Brugge, while also netting in their league victory over Crystal Palace before the international break.

Wirtz also found the back of the net in midweek in the Champions League, while he has both scored and assisted a goal in his last two Premier League appearances.

The only Liverpool player to do so three times in a row is Mohamed Salah, who did it twice, in December 2018 and October 2021.

However, Iraola believes his whole Liverpool team have made improvements on the ball in recent weeks.

"For me, it is not about Florian or Alex," said Iraola.

"If we play well, someone will score a goal, give an assist, make the numbers. It's about how those players help us play well.

"If we have a good offensive volume, someone will score the goals. We have been good in possession in the last few games, I think we are improving a lot on the ball."

“It’s a big game for everyone involved and I’m very happy to be part of it.”  https://t.co/rYdhYlcTv7

Liverpool face Everton this weekend in Iraola's first Merseyside derby since taking over from Arne Slot.

Liverpool have lost just one of their last 15 Premier League away games against Everton (W4 D10), with 10 of their last 14 visits finishing level.

"I haven't lived this derby," said the Spaniard. "But it doesn't take a lot when you are here to decide it's a big game for everybody involved.

"I am very happy to be part of it and I really hope I enjoy it. To enjoy it, there is only one way, to win the game.

"Derbies are always different. It doesn't matter where you are in the standings. Normally, the type of game is different and you can feel it from the beginning.

"We have to do our part, our duels, be at a good level. We have to know it's a derby and also be good on the ball, quality wise."

#1722. GdS: ‘A chance for Jashari’ – what Amorim expects as Modric hands over the reins

Tomorrow evening, AC Milan will entrust Ardon Jashari with the job of filling Luka Modric’s shoes, after the Croatian’s injury.

If you missed last night’s reporting, Milan have been dealt a bit of a blow ahead of their game against Olympiacos, as Modric has suffered a muscle strain. It’s not a major one, and he should be back for next weekend’s game.

Nevertheless, it creates a short-term issue and in a midfield where only a few names have convinced, it plunges Ruben Amorim into the water somewhat. There is a solution, though, and it would be ideal if he stepped up.

Since he arrived, Jashari has been seen as the next in line for Modric, but he’s never shown performances to match that eventual rise. However, Gazzetta dello Sport (as seen below) write that he could take that step against Olympiacos.

It’s a potential turning point for the Swiss, who still has the faith of the club and the fans, especially after his first goal at the weekend. So, with it being a necessity that he comes into the team here, a solid performance is needed.

It opens a space for Jashari, but filling Modric’s boots will not be an easy task. In fact, he’ll have to be at his best to replace him, especially in a game with so much on the line.

Looking at the Europa League table, the Rossoneri need to be perfect if they’re to have any chance of a top eight finish. For him, though, Jashari must be perfect if his journey at San Siro is to continue.

So far, his time in Italy has been marred by injury and a failure to establish himself as a starter, or even a key rotational option. Yet, the Diavolo never gave up on him, refusing a sale in the summer.

Now, it is time to repay that in a game where ‘everything looks different’. For Jashari, it’s a simple task: be solid. He’s got a guaranteed place, reliable teammates around him and the trust to act.

No one can challenge him for the next five days; the spot is guaranteed. It’ll be up to him if those five days become 10 or more. If not, there’s a market waiting for him.

#1721. Roberto De Zerbi handed crushing Tottenham injury blow as Savio recovery timeline now revealed

By Lewis Blain | 27 Nov 2026 07:31

Tottenham Hotspur have suffered another injury setback, with Savio expected to miss several weeks after sustaining a hamstring problem against Ipswich Town.

The Brazilian winger had only recently returned from a previous muscle injury before being forced off during last weekend's 2-0 victory in the Premier League.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi now faces the prospect of being without the winger for a significant period during a busy end to 2026.

Savio made his first appearance since the 1-1 draw with Manchester United on October 10th when he came off the bench against the Tractor Boys.

However, his return lasted only around 20 minutes, with the 22-year-old going down inside the opposition penalty area after an impressive run before being helped from the pitch by Tottenham's medical staff.

His exact recovery timeline has not yet been determined, but The Athletic report that he is now expected to miss several weeks. One source has even said Savio could miss all seven of Tottenham's remaining matches in 2026.

De Zerbi confirmed that the winger had suffered a recurrence of the same muscle injury, expressing his frustration at losing an important member of his squad.

"I'm very angry about that, because Savio is a crucial player for us," the Spurs boss said. "It's the same injury, and it is the worst thing from today."

Savio has endured a difficult start to life in north London following his summer move from Manchester City in a deal worth up to £85m. Despite scoring on his debut against Charlton Athletic, he has managed just seven appearances due to fitness problems.

Tottenham already have significant attacking concerns, with Savio joining Mathys Tel, Mykhailo Mudryk, Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert on the injury list.

The north London outfit were already expected to explore the market for a new striker, but De Zerbi may now need to consider a more versatile forward capable of operating centrally and out wide.

That would help address the lack of options on the left flank, although Savio's absence could also create opportunities for academy graduate Luca Williams-Barnett.

The 18-year-old gem scored and assisted on his first Premier League start against Ipswich, offering De Zerbi an encouraging alternative.

However, with several attacking players unavailable and Savio potentially missing the remainder of the year, adding another forward in January would make sense.

Spurs need greater depth across their frontline, and a versatile signing could help address more than one problem at once.

#1720. Tottenham XI vs Sunderland: Predicted lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest for Premier League

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Sandro Tonali has returned to training ahead of Tottenham’s visit to Sunderland, but Savio is expected to spend a significant period on the sidelines after suffering the recurrence of a hamstring injury.

Tonali missed Spurs’ 2-0 victory at home to Ipswich last weekend due to illness, but is set to be available for selection when Roberto De Zerbi’s side travel to the Stadium of Light on Sunday.

Savio, meanwhile, was named on the bench against Ipswich, having missed the previous four games. The 22-year-old was introduced in the second half, but lasted just 26 minutes before he had to come off injured.

Savio was visibly upset as he headed down the tunnel, and De Zerbi confirmed at his pre-Sunderland press conference on Friday that the Brazilian would miss the festive period.

Asked if Savio may not play again this year, De Zerbi said: “Yeah, I think [he will miss the Christmas period].

“Unfortunately it’s a tough situation to accept. He’s a new guy and he’s suffering with these new injuries. But this is football, if you see other European clubs they’re all suffering these injuries.”

De Zerbi added: “Now he needs time. He needs hard work with the medical staff. Then in 50 days, 60 days, 80 days, I don’t know, when he comes back, he will be crucial for us in the last step of the season.”

#1719. Man Utd handed huge January transfer boost as club 'desperate' to sell key Mauricio Pochettino target

By Lewis Blain | 27 Nov 2026 07:57

Manchester United could be handed a significant opportunity to strengthen their attack in January, with one of Mauricio Pochettino’s leading striker targets potentially now available.

AS Monaco are said to be 'desperate' to sell former Arsenal forward Folarin Balogun as they look to balance their books, potentially opening the door for the Red Devils to reignite their interest.

United are expected to prioritise three positions during the winter transfer window, with a new centre-forward, left-back and centre-back reportedly on Pochettino’s wishlist.

Balogun is among the strikers under consideration, with the new Man Utd manager already familiar with the USA international from their time together with the national team. The forward was arguably Pochettino’s star player at the 2026 World Cup.

United could have an opportunity to make their move after journalist Ben Jacobs, speaking to The United Stand, claimed the Ligue 1 side need to sell either Balogun or midfielder Lamine Camara in January to balance their finances.

“Monaco desperately have to sell and will have to lose one of Balogun or Camara in January,” he said.

Balogun came close to joining Everton in the summer, even travelling to Merseyside on deadline day before the proposed transfer collapsed. The Toffees could revisit their interest, although Jacobs suggested the race for his signature could be wide open.

United are also considering other options, including Victor Osimhen and Ivan Toney, but a January move for the former is considered extremely difficult.

Balogun, meanwhile, has scored twice in nine appearances across all competitions since returning from an injury that initially contributed to his failed Everton move.

United's reported transfer budget of less than £50m remains a significant obstacle, particularly with Pochettino also keen to strengthen at left-back and centre-back.

Monaco's willingness to sell could improve United's negotiating position, but it does not necessarily mean Balogun would represent a bargain. The club must also consider whether he is the right option to provide the immediate goals required.

Benjamin Sesko's persistent shin injury and Joshua Zirkzee's uncertain future have increased the need for another centre-forward, but Balogun's return of just two goals in nine games hardly makes him a guaranteed solution.

If Monaco are prepared to accept a relatively modest fee, United should seriously consider the opportunity.

However, with several positions requiring attention and limited funds available, Pochettino cannot afford to spend a significant proportion of his January budget on another forward who arrives with questions over his current form.

Bruno Fernandes, providing he overcomes an illness, will be bidding to inspire Manchester United to a win over Brentford in Saturday's Premier League clash at OId Trafford.

Fernandes has scored four goals and registered two assists in 10 Premier League appearances during the 2026-27 campaign.

Fernandes has faced Brentford on nine occasions during his career, with all of those games taking place in the top flight of English football.

#1715. Jarrod Bowen interview: I will discuss West Ham future if Premier League promotion bid fails

Jarrod Bowen has admitted that talks over his West Ham future will take place if a return to the Premier League is not secured this season.

The West Ham captain, who played his 300th game for the club this week, was the subject of Premier League interest at the end of last season following the club’s relegation to the second division for the first time in 14 years, but never considered leaving.

Bowen instead committed his immediate future to West Ham by signing a new contract, which included revised terms to help the club in their bid for promotion.

The 29-year-old says it was an easy decision to stay, but conversations will need to be had if West Ham are resigned to a second season in the second tier.

You don't want to be stuck, you want to bounce back and be in the Premier League straight away

The Hammers have endured a tricky start to life in the Championship, and currently sit outside the play-off places and winless in four games under new manager Scott Parker.

“I never wanted to leave after being relegated,” Bowen tells Standard Sport.

“I always wanted to give it an opportunity, to go we can get this club back into the Premier League. I wanted to be the spearhead of that.

Tottenham beat Arsenal to exciting transfer coup as signing confirmed

Gavin And Stacey props go to auction in aid of Cancer Research Wales

West Ham fans ‘prepare for relegation’ as pressure mounts on new manager Parker

“I think it's wrong to look too far ahead into the future because I think your energy has to be into this season. But if it doesn't happen, then we will sit down and have a conversation at the end of the season.

“But I think for now, we have to put all our energy into this season because there's something special that we can achieve.”

West Ham have struggled to adapt to the Championship, winning six of their opening 17 games, but Bowen says this came as no surprise to him and believes promotion expert Parker can turn things around.

“He's been brilliant,” Bowen says of former Hammers midfielder Parker, who has earned promotion from the Championship on three seperate occasions. “Someone who understands the club, played so many years here, captained here at this club as well. He's been a breath of fresh air since he's been here.

“We've only worked together a few weeks. Obviously, the results haven't been the way that we wanted. Some of the performances that we've had, we probably deserve more from some of the games.

“We feel we're in a weirdly good place, and we're looking forward to what we've got coming up.”

An edgy 1-0 victory at Swansea last month felt at the time like the making of West Ham as promotion candidates, but they are yet to taste victory since Parker replaced Nuno Espirito Santo in the dugout last month.

The 1-0 defeat to Portsmouth this week prompted Parker to warn that West Ham risk getting stuck in the Championship if they do not adapt to the physical demands of the league.

And Bowen insists promotion back to the top flight is not as easy as some make out.

“Of course you don't want to be stuck,” he continued. “You want to bounce back and be in the Premier League straight away, of course you do.

“But like I said, it's not as easy as what people think or just to expect. Just because you've come down, it'll be easy for you to get back promoted because that's not the case, and we're finding that out right now.”

Bowen was speaking to Standard Sport at the EFL’s Power of 72 event at the London Stadium, promoting West Ham’s Thrive employability programme, which concentrates on providing support to Neet (not in education, employment or training) and underemployed young people in Newham and east London.

EFL Power of 72 celebrates the positive impact EFL Clubs have on their communities and the bond between clubs and local people, with one million people participating in EFL club charity programmes every season.

“It's so important to me because it's something that I've been involved in for a few years now since I've been here,” Bowen said of the Thrive employability programme.

“We have people with different backgrounds, different upbringings, that all have limited opportunities to go out and showcase that. So, the work we're doing is giving them the opportunity to go and showcase what they want to do, giving them the work experience to go on and achieve what they set out to do.”

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta has urged his Arsenal players to block out all talk of Manchester City’s Premier League charges and ensure they win the title on the pitch.

In September, City were were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018, while an independent commission also ruled that the club failed to co-operate with an investigation.

It is a shadow hanging over the league ahead of Arsenal’s showdown with City in north London on Sunday.

Victory would move the Gunners nine points ahead of Enzo Maresca’s side and leave them in strong shape to defend their league title, regardless of any potential sanctions imposed on City.

Arteta is clear that his players cannot afford any distractions, demanding that they get the job done and defend their crown without relying on a potential points deduction for City.

“That’s the only thing that we should put the energy and the focus on,” Arteta said. “There’s nothing else.”

Arsenal were defeated twice by City in the space of three weeks towards the end of last season, first in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley and then in a Premier League clash at the Etihad Stadium. Despite losing the latter game, Arsenal went on to win the title for the first time in 22 years.

A rivalry has built between the two clubs over the past five seasons, having gone toe-to-toe in several title races.

Asked if the guilty verdict against City and the wait for possible sanctions had diminished the significance of Sunday’s meeting, Arteta said: “I hope that it doesn’t because it’s a process that is still open.

However, when it was put to him that the atmosphere might be particularly emotional due to the strength of feeling from the Arsenal fans, Arteta sidestepped the topic.

“I don’t know,” he said. “That’s something very individual and I don’t want to go there.”

#1713. Chelsea's slump in form unpacked: The stars who badly need to step up from Emi Martinez to Cole Palmer, what defensive horror shows mean for Xabi Alonso's job security - and the players in line to leave in January

Published: 12:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:02 EST, 23 November 2026

Chelsea are lurching towards a crisis after yet another loss in which they were bullied, this time by Leeds United.

That 4-1 hiding saw Xabi Alonso heckled, and his players booed at both half-time and full-time, arguably deservedly so for such a disastrous showing.

It has led to tentative speculation around Alonso's future as Chelsea prepare to travel to Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest on Friday night, not to mention questions about where he is going wrong and how he might arrest his team's slump in form.

Here, Daily Mail Sport tackles all the burning issues at Stamford Bridge...

Chief among Chelsea’s problems is the fact they have conceded 20 Premier League goals this season. It is as many as they have scored at the other end. So, as much as we have enjoyed their freescoring forward line this season, so too must we criticise their disastrous defending.

We know Alonso can organise a defence. His Bayer Leverkusen side only conceded 24 goals when they won the Bundesliga as unbeaten champions in 2023-24. Chelsea are now on the verge of overtaking that total before we even hit December.

Liam Delap, their former striker now at Forest, will be desperate to add to that tally this Friday, too.

Xabi Alonso is coming under growing pressure, with his Chelsea side failing to back up their promising early-season form

Levi Colwill was all at sea against Leeds as Chelsea shipped another four goals, taking their tally to 20 in 11 games

This morning, I watched back all 20 of the goals that Chelsea have leaked this term. There have been so many individual mistakes.

Like on day one, in the 3-2 win at Fulham, when an out of position Robert Sanchez let in Josh King's shot. And when Levi Colwill missed a defensive header which should have been routine, which led to Gonzalo Garcia scoring.

Chelsea got rid of Sanchez after that game, but Emiliano Martinez has hardly helped shore up this defence, as was apparent in the 4-1 loss to Leeds, when Colwill and Co were again all over the shop.

Until they cut out the silly mistakes, it is hard to see Chelsea competing at the top end of the Premier League.

Every manager at every club is sackable. Nobody is immune. But that’s not to say Alonso is suddenly up for the chop at Chelsea. I haven’t heard anything which would suggest those inside the club think finding a fourth permanent manager in the year 2026 is the answer.

Let’s not forget the overwhelming optimism when news broke of Chelsea striking an agreement to hire Alonso. It was an hour or so after the club had lost the 2026 FA Cup final to Manchester City. Recently, I took a look at the comments section of the story I wrote that day. It was full of excitement from Chelsea fans, and anger from Liverpool supporters at missing out on him.

Anyway, I think it’s too soon for us to start talking about Alonso’s job. He is in a bad moment, obviously. A very bad moment. Losing at home to Tottenham Hotspur and Leeds is a complete no-no for any Blues boss.

The supporters are more likely to curse his name than chant it right now, and it is hard to identify the style Alonso wants, with few discernible patterns of play to Chelsea's football.

But let’s give the bloke a chance to get himself out of this jam as he heads into his 12th Premier League match.

Believe it or not, Chelsea don’t like changing managers mid-season if they can help it. Enzo Maresca resigned, exiting on January 1, 2026. Liam Rosenior was sacked, yes, but the club were effectively forced into that change as the players clearly gave up on him. Let’s see if Alonso can find some solutions.

Chelsea don’t like changing managers mid-season if they can help it and Alonso, remember, has only had 11 Premier League games in charge

We’ve tried to coax a little anger out of Alonso at press conferences, practically encouraging him to have a pop at his players for how they are performing, but he tends to resist the urge.

He’s clearly a nice guy. However, a Chelsea source does tell me he’s different behind the scenes. We may not see it on the outside, but internally, he is perfectly capable of being fiery with the players.

Which I hope is the case. Because sometimes, it can feel as if these Chelsea players need a good kick up the backside, rather than being coddled.

I wrote a piece after the 4-1 loss to Leeds about how superstars can be stroppy. It’s normal. They can be so good that when the game isn’t going their way, they show their sulky side.

Palmer did that both during and after Saturday’s defeat. It was pretty poor from him to not want to go around applauding the fans who had bothered to stick around at full-time, even if there had been boos. An apology has been attributed to Palmer on social media, but that’s just another case of fake quotes being circulated.

For me, Palmer has to look at himself as much as anybody. It’s been too long since we’ve seen him try to take a match by the scruff of the neck.

Cole Palmer put in another quiet display against Leeds - he needs to start taking matches by the scruff of the neck

WHAT HAPPENED WITH EMEGHA AFTER THE GAME?

Striker Emmanuel Emegha started for the first time and scored for the first time in Chelsea’s 4-1 loss to Leeds. Then he exited Stamford Bridge.

We have seen players leaving the stadium on foot before. Videos of Palmer being surrounded by supporters while being escorted to his ride home occasionally crop up on social media.

Emegha had possessions stolen from his car while he was in a restaurant after the match and the incident has been reported to police. He was not harmed.

From a footballing point of view, I'd like to see Emegha start away at Forest this Friday.

Not that I’m aware. He’s been linked with Paris Saint-Germain and I had an email from a PR person this morning trying to push a loan to AC Milan or Roma as a possibility.

Alonso has given the fans what they wanted in the last few league games. He started Estevao against Manchester United, brought him on at half-time at Sunderland and started him against Leeds.

Estevao, clearly an exciting talent, could do with taking these opportunities to show why he deserves more of them.

Estevao has been given a chance to shine by Alonso in recent weeks but has failed to grab his opportunities

I could see Malo Gusto leaving if there’s interest and Chelsea don’t keep demanding £75million, because it is hard to see who would spend that on him.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign. Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in the loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

I wouldn’t be surprised if a few other fringe players are linked with leaving in pursuit of game time ahead of January, such as Valentin Barco and Jamie Gittens, who is training again after his ankle injury.

As for incomings, I don’t need to tell you that Chelsea are interested in Alex Scott of Bournemouth. Arsenal are, too, but the word is the Blues are still the frontrunners as we approach January. Whether Scott is what this team needs is another conversation.

#1712. Liverpool suspension risks: Key duo walking Premier League tightrope before Chelsea clash

Liverpool are looking up as the hectic period of the campaign approaches.

Andoni Iraola's side have bounced back from successive defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce prior to the November international break, and go into the Everton game seeking a fourth straight win across all competitions.

While Sunday’s showdown at the Hill Dickinson Stadium will represent Iraola’s first taste of a Merseyside derby, history largely favours the Reds having lost just one of the last 10 meetings.

It remains to be seen if Victor Munoz is able to shake off a knock and prove his fitness, but two key Liverpool players will have to be careful if selected due to the looming threat of a ban.

With that in mind, here’s a look at the Liverpool players at risk of suspension.

As every club have already been made fully aware of this season, players who pick up five yellow cards in the first 19 matches of the Premier League season are hit with a one-match ban.

Liverpool's cut-off point in which suspensions will be handed out for a fifth yellow card is the home game against Coventry on January 2, 2027. From there, players who are booked 10 times in the first 32 matches of the campaign are suspended for two games.

Alexis Mac Allister and summer signing Bradley Barcola are the big suspensions concern for Liverpool at present.

The Argentina international was booked in the win over Crystal Palace so had to watch his step in the 4-0 thrashing of Manchester United, but Barcola is a new suspension risk after being cautioned in the second half last weekend.

As such, if the Frenchman and/or Mac Allister are shown a yellow card in the Merseyside derby, a one-match ban must be served in the very next fixture - at home to Sunderland on December 2.

Ultimately, the pair are walking the disciplinary tightrope for upcoming games against Everton, Sunderland, Chelsea, Leeds, Tottenham, Hull, Aston Villa and Coventry.

Furthermore, with Liverpool taking on Chelsea next weekend, Barcola and/or Mac Allister would be suspended for the trip to Stamford Bridge if either are booked against the Black Cats.

Ronald Araujo, Milos Kerkez and Virgil van Dijk are on three yellow cards, while Jeremy Jacquet and Munoz are among a host of Liverpool players still in danger of being suspended.

Manchester United will be aiming to win for just the second time in the Premier League this season when they welcome Brentford to Old Trafford.

UK viewers can also watch the highlights of the game on Match of the Day, which will start at 10:30pm on BBC One and run until 11:30pm.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a disastrous Premier League campaign to date for the 20-time English champions, who were thumped 4-0 at Liverpool last weekend.

The Bees will enter the match off the back of a 4-0 win over Everton, and they currently sit sixth in the table, only one point off fifth-placed Bournemouth.

#1709. Maher optimistic Nashville can turn MLS Cup playoff tie against Cincinnati around

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Nashville SC defender Jack Maher revealed he is "so confident" his team-mates can defeat FC Cincinnati in their MLS Cup playoff tie.

Nashville won the 2026 Supporters' Shield in stunning fashion, setting a new single-season points record (77), but made a losing start to the postseason.

BJ Callaghan's side lost Game 1 in Round One at home 1-0 after an early own goal from Patrick Yazbek, marking their first defeat at GEODIS Park in MLS play this season.

Nashville must now defeat Cincinnati in Game 2 on Saturday to keep the series alive, and Maher is optimistic they can get the job done at TQL Stadium.

"First loss at home in MLS play for the whole entire year, and I think that that's something that clearly is frustrating," said Maher.

"The mood around the locker room was that this hasn't really happened before this year. But we're optimistic about the next game, and we're going to give it clearly everything we got.

"It's a hungry group in that locker room, and I think that if [Cincinnati] want to go on, they got to beat us twice.

"I'm so confident that we have the guys in this locker room to be able to go up to Cincinnati, get a great result, come back home, and finish the job."

Nashville boss Callaghan added: "This team's battle-tested, and the group will be ready to respond.

"You can feel that there's a bit of a hunger. This team has continually showed that we have the experience from early in the season in playing knockout-type games, and the group will be prepared to respond."

Evander was held without a shot or a chance created in the Game 1 victory.

Over his eight MLS seasons, Hany Mukhtar has scored 37 goals and added 28 assists on the road in MLS play (including playoffs).

His 65 away goal contributions make him one of two MLS players with at least 60 goal contributions on the road since 2020, along with Carles Gil (71).

The winner was the second time this season Cincinnati benefited from an own goal (the final goal in a 3-3 draw at Chicago in April). The own goal in Game 1 was the first playoff own goal from outside the box over the last 20 seasons.

The Game 1 loss ended a 10-match unbeaten streak against MLS opponents for Nashville (W7 D3). They have not lost consecutive matches in MLS play since October 2025, when they dropped their regular-season finale and playoff opener, both to Inter Miami.

#1708. Manchester United have new suspension risk after Leny Yoro red card appeal

Manchester United will have Leny Yoro available for selection against Brentford this weekend, though a fellow defender remains at risk of a Premier League suspension.

Yoro was dismissed after just eight minutes in Man United’s defeat to Liverpool last Sunday, as Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge after succeeding Michael Carrick as head coach quickly turned into a nightmare.

The Frenchman was given his marching orders for bringing down Alexander Isak just outside the box, with the Premier League revealing the red card was shown to the United defender “for denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO)”.

However, Man Utd appealed the decision and it has proven successful with Yoro cleared to face Brentford on Saturday.

A statement from the FA read: “Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a claim of wrongful dismissal.

“The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.”

Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a claim of wrongful dismissal

United have had to deal with their fair share of suspensions already this season. Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Matheus Cunha and, more recently, Youri Tielemans, have all been sent-off at some point to raise concerns over a disciplinary issue within the squad.

A further suspension concern is in the form of central defender Harry Maguire, who is currently on four Premier League yellow cards.

As per the rules, players who pick up five yellow cards in the first 19 matches of the Premier League season are hit with a one-match ban.

Man United's cut-off point in which suspensions will be handed out for a fifth yellow card is the away game against Brighton on January 2, 2027. From there, players who are booked 10 times in the first 32 matches of the campaign are suspended for two games.

#1707. Deportivo La Coruna vs. Barcelona: Head-to-head record and past meetings ahead of La Liga clash

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 08:20, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 08:23

Barcelona will continue their La Liga campaign against Deportivo La Coruna on Sunday afternoon.

Hansi Flick's side are top of the La Liga table on 36 points, three points ahead of second-placed Real Madrid, while Deportivo are 12th in the division.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides ahead of their clash this weekend.

Barcelona and Deportivo have locked horns on 105 previous occasions throughout history, and it is the former that leads the overall head-to-head record 63 wins to 22, while 20 of their encounters have ended all square.

Lionel Messi is the all-time leading goalscorer in matches between Barcelona and Deportivo, having scored 20 times in this fixture while representing the Catalan giants.

Barcelona have scored 258 times against Deportivo, conceding 112, while they also comfortably lead the La Liga head-to-head 53 victories to Deportivo's 21.

Four of the last five meetings between the two sides have been won by Barcelona, including 4-0 and 4-2 successes during the 2017-18 La Liga campaign.

Deportivo do have a recent victory over Barcelona to their name, having posted a 2-1 win on home soil in March 2017, but they have only beaten Barcelona once since April 2008.

The Blue and Whites have twice enjoyed three-game winning runs against Barcelona throughout history - between October 2000 and October 2001, and then again between November 2002 and October 2003.

Moises Caicedo starts for Chelsea in tonight’s Premier League clash against Nottingham Forest.

Winger Jamie Gittens, meanwhile, has been building his fitness of late having resumed training following an ankle injury.

#1704. The World Cup RETURNS to America! FIFA announces 2031 tournament hosts after historic four-country bid

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 10:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 13:19 EST, 23 November 2026

The World Cup is set to return to America after FIFA awarded the 2031 women's tournament to a historic four-nation bid.

Following the success of the men's tournament this summer, the United States was announced as one of the hosts of the women's edition in five years' time during a virtual meeting of FIFA's national associations on Monday.

The US will co-host the global soccer extravaganza alongside Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica after the four countries' joint bid was awarded uncontested the 2031 tournament.

The selection marks a milestone for the Women's World Cup with the tournament being hosted across four nations for the first time in its history.

The last World Cup was co-hosted by multiple countries for the first time with the 2023 edition taking place across Australia and New Zealand.

This summer's men's World Cup was also co-hosted by the US with games taking place across the States, Canada and Mexico.

The World Cup is set to return to the United States for the 2031 women's edition of the event

Spain are reigning champions after winning the Women's World Cup in 2023

The United States Women's National Team are four-time winners in 1991, 1999, 2015 and 2019

The 2031 tournament will also be the largest in the competition's history, featuring an expanded 48-team field and 104 matches for the first time.

'We are incredibly honored and excited to welcome the world to the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica for the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup,' said US Soccer President Cindy Parlow Cone.

'This is a historic moment for our four countries, but the opportunity is much bigger than any one of us. Together with FIFA, we want to deliver the biggest and most impactful Women's World Cup in history and use its success to accelerate the growth of women's soccer around the world. Our ambition is to create a tournament that not only inspires millions of players, but helps give them the opportunities to play, grow and pursue their dreams.'

The selection marks the third time that the Women's World Cup has been awarded to the US with the country previously hosting the landmark 1999 and 2003 editions alone. The national team's tournament win in 1999 was the second of its four titles.

Meanwhile, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will become first-time hosts at the historic tournament.

'This milestone furthers the continued belief that the best days of soccer in America are still ahead,' said U.S. Soccer CEO and General Secretary JT Batson.

'We have an opportunity to use the momentum from the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup to accelerate our ambitions for the future of soccer, from expanding access and participation to strengthening the pathways that develop the next generation of players. We are excited to work alongside our partners across the region to make this tournament a defining moment for women's soccer.'

The U.S.-led 2031 project across the CONCACAF regional soccer body bid offers FIFA a choice of stadiums in 20 cities: 14 in the U.S., four in Mexico plus San José in Costa Rica and Kingston, Jamaica.

US Soccer President Cindy Parlow Cone said the federation was honored to be selected

The host selection of the 2035 Women's World Cup was awarded to a joint bid between England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales

The host selection of the 2035 Women's World Cup was also announced on Monday with the tournament being awarded to another joint bid between England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

It marks the first time that a World Cup has been hosted on the British Isles since the men's tournament in 1966 in England.

The United Kingdom bid joins England with Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales that offers a choice from 19 venues, including Wembley Stadium in London.

The winning candidates and FIFA president Gianni Infantino promised commercially successful tournaments - the first editions with 48 teams and 104 games - and to reinvest all that money in women's soccer.

FIFA wanted these heavyweights of women's soccer to face no opposition without rival bids and so lead hosting the first expanded tournaments. That will bring parity with the men's World Cup which expanded to 48 teams this year in the US, Canada and Mexico.

The 2027 Women's World Cup will have 32 teams in Brazil.

#1703. Will Man City be stripped of Premier League titles? Possible sanctions amid new update before Arsenal showdown

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal take on Manchester City in the standout Premier League fixture this weekend, though it will be played in the backdrop of uncertainty.

While it is first against third and a showdown between last season’s top two, the outcome at the Emirates Stadium may not have too much of an impact on this year’s title race.

This is because Man City head to north London on the back of being handed an update on their appeal against the Premier League's financial charges.

Back in October, City were in October found guilty of 114 breaches of the league's financial rules, with an independent commission concluding the club had used "sham" commercial contracts to disguise more than £830million in funding between 2009 and 2018.

City, however, have consistently denied wrongdoing, and an appeal was immediately launched with a result expected in early 2027.

Speculation over possible punishments, should Man City’s appeal prove unsuccessful, range from a fine to various points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League.

Meanwhile, senior figures at some Premier League clubs have told BBC Sport that Man City’s owners must be forced to sell up as punishment for its breaking financial rules.

Below is a breakdown of what sanctions Man City could potentially face if their appeal is unsuccessful.

Expulsion from the Premier League: The most severe sanction could see Man City removed from the Premier League and relegated to the Championship, with any decision subject to the relevant league rules and the outcome of any appeal.

Suspension from Premier League matches: Another potential sanction would be a suspension. The club could potentially be suspended from participating in Premier League fixtures for a specified period.

Liverpool handed new suspension risk ahead of Chelsea clash

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

Points deduction: A significant deduction in points could be imposed, either during the current season or in a future campaign.

The size and timing of any deduction would be determined as part of the sanctions process.

Stripping of titles and trophies: Retrospective sporting penalties could also potentially affect honours that were won during the period covered by the charges.

In this scenario, Arsenal would not be awarded a single retrospective Premier League title. This is because the seasons in which they finished runners-up to Man City has not been under investigation. The Gunners would, though get a League Cup after being demolished 3-0 by City in the 2017-18 final at Wembley.

However, no decision has been made to strip City of any titles or trophies.

Transfer restrictions: The club could potentially face restrictions on registering or signing players for one or more transfer windows.

Fines: City could also face substantial financial penalties. The club could be ordered to pay fines, compensation or costs associated with the proceedings.

The sanctions process is separate from the commission’s determination on the charges, meaning City’s punishment remains to be decided.

#1702. Deportivo La Coruna vs Barcelona - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 08:25, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 08:29

Barcelona will bid to post a sixth straight win in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign against Deportivo La Coruna at Estadio Riazor on Sunday afternoon.

The Catalan giants have won four of their last five matches against Deportivo, including a famous 8-0 success in the corresponding game during the 2015-16 campaign.

Deportivo boast a record of three wins, six draws and four defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 15 points leaving them in 12th position in the La Liga table.

The Blue and Whites finished second in last season's Segunda Division table to secure a return to the top flight, and their opening to this campaign has certainly been positive.

Antonio Hidalgo's side will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 defeat to Alaves, but they have picked up four points from their last three games at this level, including a 2-1 success over Osasuna in their last game in front of their own fans on November 2.

Deportivo have picked up nine points from their six home league matches this season, and their last success over Barcelona did come in front of their own fans - a 2-1 win in March 2017.

These two teams have locked horns on 105 previous occasions throughout history, and it is Barcelona that leads the overall head-to-head record 63 wins to Deportivo's 22, while 20 of their encounters have finished all square.

Barcelona will enter this match off the back of a 4-1 win over Sabah in the Champions League, with the result leaving Hansi Flick's side in fourth spot in the overall table on 12 points.

While the Catalan giants are in an excellent position to secure a spot in the knockout round of the Champions League, they also sit at the top of the La Liga table, picking up 36 points from their 13 matches courtesy of a record of 12 wins and one defeat.

Barcelona are three points ahead of second-placed Real Madrid and five clear of third-placed Atletico Madrid, and they posted a 3-2 success over Villarreal in their last league fixture.

The Blaugrana have the best home record in La Liga this season, picking up 18 points from seven matches, while they are comfortably the highest goalscorers in Spain's top flight during the 2026-27 campaign, finding the back of the net on 51 occasions.

Barcelona now have three straight league matches against Deportivo, Atletico Madrid and Celta Vigo before resuming their Champions League campaign against Manchester City on December 8.

Deportivo La Coruna form (all competitions):

Deportivo's squad is in strong shape at the moment in terms of availability, although Bright Ede (hamstring) and Zakaria Eddahchouri (wrist) remain major doubts for the home side.

Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang has scored five times in La Liga this season and is set to continue through the middle despite the fact that he is three games without a goal since returning from a knee injury at the start of November.

Mariano Soriano and Luismi Cruz have both scored twice for Deportivo this season, meanwhile, and the pair are set to continue in the starting side.

As for Barcelona, Lamine Yamal was absent against Sabah in the Champions League on Wednesday due to a minor ankle injury, but the Spain international is set to return to the starting side for this weekend's contest.

There will be no Fermin Lopez, though, following the attacker's red card against Villarreal last time out; Roony Bardghji (knee) and Xavi Espart (ankle) are also definitely out of the clash.

However, Rodri and Andreas Christensen both have chances of being back in the squad.

The ankle injury that Alejandro Balde suffered against Sabah is not serious, meanwhile, so the left-back could potentially make the squad.

Eric Garcia, Pau Cubarsi, Joao Cancelo, Dani Olmo and Raphinha could also all be brought into the starting team following the European clash with Sabah.

Deportivo La Coruna possible starting lineup:

Roman; Navarro, Noubi, Loureiro, Quagliata; Luismi, Soriano, Casado, Rodriguez, Hernandez; Aubameyang

J Garcia; E Garcia, Cubarsi, Martin, Cancelo; Bernal, Pedri; Yamal, Olmo, Gordon; Raphinha

This is a really tough ask for Deportivo against a quality Barcelona outfit - we are backing the hosts to score, but Flick's side should be able to navigate their way to all three points.

#1701. Bastoni could miss remainder of 2026 as Inter gear up for Genoa double header

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Inter centre-back Alessandro Bastoni has suffered a left quadriceps strain, with reports indicating he will miss Saturday's meeting with Genoa and may not return until 2027.

The Nerazzurri confirmed on Friday that Bastoni had undergone tests in the wake of Wednesday's 2-0 Champions League victory over Stuttgart, in which Bastoni only lasted 41 minutes before being replaced by Federico Dimarco.

Bastoni has made 15 appearances for Inter across all competitions, with all 15 of those being starts. The only outfielder to better his 1,199 minutes for Cristian Chivu's side in 2026-27 is midfielder Nicolo Barella (1,298).

Bastoni has won 45 of the 79 duels he has contested this term, including 14 of 20 in the air, helping Inter win 29 points from the first 12 games of their Scudetto defence.

A club statement said: "Alessandro Bastoni underwent clinical and diagnostic tests this morning at the Humanitas Institute in Rozzano.

"The tests revealed a strain to his left quadriceps."

Inter did not offer a timeline for Bastoni's recovery, but with widespread reports indicating he could miss at least three weeks, he may not return until the new year.

Inter have seven games to play before New Year's Eve, the last of which is a Supercoppa Italiana final showdown with Lazio on December 22, a little over three weeks away.

Despite Inter's strong points haul, they sit third in Serie A ahead of Genoa's visit to San Siro, behind Lazio and Roma.

Yet Chivu was impressed by his players' reaction against Stuttgart in midweek, after their previous game saw them squander a 4-2 lead in a 4-4 draw with Atalanta.

"We didn't lose clarity of mind after the game in Bergamo: we played well for 75 minutes, but the final stages don't define the good things we produced in that match," he said.

"To tell the truth, you have to remain clear-headed and analyse what happened from a technical and mental point of view."

Inter will face Genoa twice in the space of three days, with the teams also being drawn together in the Coppa Italia's round of 16. The Grifone are 10th in Serie A, having beaten Sassuolo 2-0 away from home last time out.

Esposito, at the age of 21 years and 147 days, became the fourth-youngest player to score 12+ Serie A goals for Inter in the three-points-for-a-win era last week, behind Mario Balotelli (19 years and 78 days), Obafemi Martins (20 years and 17 days) and Ronaldo Nazario (21 years and 146 days).

If he scores a brace here (21 years and 153 days old on Saturday), he would become the third-youngest to reach 15 goals for the Nerazzurri, surpassing Ronaldo, who achieved this milestone at 21 years and 159 days.

Osmajic has scored six goals in his first 12 Serie A appearances since arriving from Preston North End.

Among players in their debut Serie A seasons, in the three-points-for-a-win era, only Diego Milito (11 in 2008-09) and Krzysztof Piatek (10 in 2018-19) have netted more goals in the first 13 games of a campaign for Genoa.

Inter are unbeaten in their last 14 Serie A matches against Genoa (W11 D3). Among current top-flight teams, they only have a longer ongoing unbeaten run against Atalanta (16).

At home, meanwhile, the Nerazzurri have posted 12 straight league wins over Genoa, keeping a clean sheet in 10 of those games and only conceding two goals in total.

Throughout their top-flight history, Inter have only registered a longer run of successive home wins against Como (15).

Inter's firepower should prove too much for Genoa here, too, as they have scored in each of their last 22 Serie A matches, netting 57 times in total at an average of 2.6 per game.

They have also won six in a row at home in Serie A, scoring at least two goals in each of those matches.

The Nerazzurri last enjoyed a longer Serie A winning streak at San Siro between October 2023 and March 2024 (nine in a row), while they last had a longer run while scoring multiple goals in every game between October 2016 and February 2017 (eight in a row).

#1700. Mauricio Pochettino calls up forgotten Manchester United signing to training ahead of home debut

Enzo Kana-Biyik has trained with the Manchester United senior squad ahead of this weekend’s Premier League showdown against Brentford.

Man United welcome the Bees to Old Trafford on Saturday seeking a first league victory since August in what will be Mauricio Pochettino’s home debut as head coach.

The Red Devils go into the game in the relegation zone, but can climb out of the bottom three - albeit potentially temporarily - with victory coupled with Ipswich losing at home to Aston Villa.

Man Utd’s hopes of repeating the result from their last meeting with Brentford have been boosted with Leny Yoro available for selection after his red card against Liverpool was overturned on appeal.

However, captain Bruno Fernandes is a doubt with illness which means he could be absent alongside Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte.

"Yes, we don't know," Pochettino revealed in the pre-match press conference. "He's affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and, today, he cannot be part of the training session.

"We'll see. We are going to see during the day and tomorrow, how he wakes up, and we'll see. We're not going to take any risks, because you know when this type of situation happens, you don't feel [you can].

"We are going to pay attention but, still, we decide nothing."

With some senior players absence from training on Friday, it allowed for a couple of youngsters to be called up by Pochettino.

This included Jack and Tyler Fletcher, Jim Thwaites and Jaydan Kamason. Though, perhaps the most notable inclusion was that of highly-rated French forward Kana-Biyik.

The 19-year-old joined Man United in July 2025 after the Red Devils had won the race to sign the wonderkid on a free transfer from Le Havre in April of that year.

#1698. “If there can be a way out” – Moretto states Milan have no intention of offering Tomori a renewal

It seems we are heading into the final year of Fikayo Tomori’s playing relationship with AC Milan, with talk of a renewal silent.

Next year, at the end of June, Tomori’s deal expires and if nothing is done before then, his six-year spell with the club will come to an end.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s been an up-and-down season for the Englishman, especially after he was included in the ‘bomb squad’ through the mercato. However, he was needed back in the squad and reintegrated.

Despite showing this fight, though, it seems unlikely that he’ll be rewarded with a new deal. There are plans to invest heavily in the club next year and the defender isn’t seen as a pillar of the team, let alone the defence. So a renewal isn’t being focused on.

As Matteo Moretto told viewers on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, Tomori previously had a chance at a renewal. However, that now seems to have gone, as MilanNews relays.

“There’s a before and after regarding Tomori. In my opinion, if Massimiliano Allegri had remained on the Milan bench, perhaps in that case there could have been a chance of a renewal for Tomori.

“Then there was the slightly peculiar way Milan handled the Tomori situation. Tomori is a player who has always been absolutely professional and deeply loves the Milan shirt; he has always shown all his commitment.

“It’s true, he was sidelined; Milan tried to find solutions on the way out right in the last days of the transfer window. His contract expires in 2027.

“There were discussions underway for the renewal when Allegri was on the bench; then, with time and with the succession of certain events, this type of renewal was no longer discussed.

“To date, the negotiations are absolutely at a standstill. There is no dialogue between the parties and I repeat, Tomori’s contract expires in 2027.

“We’ll see if in January there can be a way out, perhaps with the payment of compensation to Milan, or if it will reach zero in June, but as of today there is no trace of a possible renewal.”
