#1645. How Arsenal are evolving their build-up play

Arsenal have evolved how they attack this season. I think there have been quite a few improvements in the way Arsenal seek to create danger that haven’t necessarily shown up on the score board so far. This is an especially sensitive subject this week after draws with Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund- games where Arsenal took deserved one goal leads but failed to build on them.

However, the failure to add true ceiling raising talent in attack this summer- despite heavy interest in Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez- has led to Mikel Arteta needing to coach his way out of a tight spot. The manager has made some alterations to his materials to make Arsenal’s final third play less austere this season. Here are some ways Arteta has evolved the team’s approach play.

Rotations and fluidity Under Mikel Arteta we are accustomed to seeing the left-back enjoy a role based on improvisation and freedom. Last season, we began to see Jurrien Timber take up some very advanced roles from right-back. This stands to reason because full-backs are not typically assigned a marker by the opposition, so it’s easier for full-backs to pop up hither and thither in advanced areas without detection.

That license has been extended this season. Let’s look at some examples just from the Newcastle game. David Raya launches a long pass here and *squints* who is that playing the role of target man and bringing the long ball down at centre-forward? By God THAT’S EBERECHI EZE’S MUSIC?!

And look who that is sprinting up beside him in the number 10 position but right-back Jurrien Timber. Madueke has a shot and hits the post from this build-up. Look at where Timber is when Madueke takes the shot.

Then we see Odegaard at left-centre-back here (sure, what the hell?) and whose buccaneering forward run is that he is picking out?

Why it’s Riccardo Calafiori. Spotting where Jurrien Timber is when Arsenal have shots on goal has become a favourite pastime of mine. Where’s Jurrien in this shot?

Here he is running down the left-wing to tee Havertz up for a shot.

This is how the move starts for the Eze goal. Konsa at right-back, Timber at centre-back, Calafiori in central midfield.

When Konsa clips the ball forwards, Madueke has shown for the ball centrally like a number 9 while Havertz has pulled into Madueke’s position. Calafiori continues his run like a horse trotting along without a jockey. You get the message by now, Madueke’s goal in the second half sees Timber make a pass to Havertz in left central midfield.

One of Arsenal’s first shots of the season is created by Tzolis drifting over to the right wing and we had seen Saka manipulated into all sorts of shooting positions prior to his injury. Tzolis was also frustratingly caught offside at St. James’ Park when he had drifted over to the right wing. Hincapie spent a lot of time in central midfield against Borussia Dortmund. Arsenal are a far more fluid outfit this season.

This sense of shapeshifting is reflected in midfield. Rice and Odegaard pretty much always start, the identity of the third midfielder can be any one of Bruno, Lewis Skelly, Zubimendi and Merino, all of whom are high level players with very different qualities. Just the identity of those names gives you face value options.

Declan Rice leads the Premier League for assists this season and all of them have been from open play. That alone tells you something different is happening. Roles in midfield are less defined. There were probably times last season when the Rice and Zubimendi combination became a little too ‘side to side’ and not cutting enough. Spending lots of money on 28-year-old Bruno tells you what Arteta felt his midfield was missing last season- risk and thrust.

Bruno expanded on this in the pre-Dortmund press conference, he spoke about the midfield at Arsenal being far less defined positionally, where Rice, Odegaard and AN Other (usually Bruno) will freelance between the 6, 8 and 10 positions. ‘It’s very different. When I was at Newcastle, you play more positional, keep more your position. Here it’s a little bit more free.

‘If you see the game against Newcastle, they were marking us man to man. You see JT [Jurrien Timber] plays a six, an eight and a number nine sometimes, so you have to move a lot. Of course, I was not used to it. So now I understand a little bit more what he wants for the midfield.’ I expanded on midfield a little more in my column from two weeks ago.

Arsenal have not been able to land a genuinely elite attacker in what feels like years now. Fortunately, Arsenal have a manager who might be the best in the trade at this moment in time. As well as moving to a more freestyle approach all over the pitch, there have been signs of improvement in individuals.

Firstly, Noni Madueke seems to be thriving on the opportunities afforded him by Saka’s recent injury. He looks more confident, his actions have greater clarity and Arsenal have treated Madueke as if he is Saka, that is to say, they give him the ball at every opportunity and rely on Noni’s capacity for repetition.

He is averaging 3.28 shots per 90 in the Premier League this season compared to 1.85 per 90 last season. (He is also averaging fewer crosses per 90 this season which implies an increasing willingness to vary his play and drive at goal as often as he does the by-line). His pass completion rate has jumped by 10% on last season.

The goal against Dortmund saw Madueke cushion a long pass, kill it perfectly and shift it to Gyokeres, who turns and lashes the ball home from 25 yards. That is not a goal description I could have envisaged in September. Gyokeres started the season very badly indeed.

Lewis touched on Gyokeres’ increased creativity this season during the international break. It looks to me as though there has been a focus on him being allowed to offload the ball after one or two touches. You don’t really want the ball getting bogged down with Gyokeres, the more touches he requires the more his technical limitations will show.

Gyokeres gets the ball from a Raya kick here and Madueke is nice and close to him and running in behind.

It means Gyokeres can take one touch and then play in behind. We see something very similar for the chance he creates for Havertz away at Brighton, Havertz is already moving when the ball comes to Gyokeres and it means he can take one touch and hook it in behind.

Then there is his lovely one-touch assist for Declan Rice in Munich where, again, he has a runner very close to him and it allows him to play the ball first time.

Arsenal have also been working on getting Eze in behind and through on goal, look at his position here when Odegaard plays a through ball in Munich.

And look at where he is when he slots Havertz’s lovely slide-rule pass at St. James’ Park.

Getting Eze in on the shoulder of the opposition right-back is another move we are seeing bear fruit sporadically. This fits into a wider theme I touched on a fortnight ago about Arsenal going in behind more often and more quickly this season.

#1644. Pointless points to play for

There’s not much going on yet, but of course we have a game against Man City on Sunday. Typically this is a fixture which would mean a lot in a season, but this time around, given the pending judgement after their appeal for being found guilty on 114 of the 115 charges, it doesn’t really feel that way.

I see their fixtures and even the latest run of poor results doesn’t connect in the same way it would have done in seasons gone by. I wonder how different it is for the players and the manager. I guess they have to be professional and do the job in front of them. Regardless of what kind of punishment is handed out to City in due course, there are three points to play for on Sunday.

But if they are punished the way they should be, it feels like this game – along with all their other games – just shouldn’t matter. When I wrote about this at the time, I said this was something of an existential issue for the Premier League, and that’s still how I think about it. We have a club who have cheated, lied, obstructed, and damaged the competition itself just going through the motions until such time as they receive a points deduction or an expulsion or a transfer ban or all of those things, and it kind of feels pointless (three points aside etc etc haha).

We still don’t know when that’s going to happen, but if it does come down mid-season, how can we look at this campaign as one which is fair? I suppose that very much applies to many of the seasons in which they actually won the league, because they did it thanks to their cheating, but surely pre-decision games against City and post-decision games are not going to be the same in terms of their competitiveness. That’s a problem, but one I hope doesn’t preclude something happening sooner rather than later because despite how quiet it’s gone around them, this issue hangs over this season’s Premier League like a toxic cloud.

I suppose if there is an upside about this fixture right now, it’s that we no longer have to endure questions about Mikel Arteta and his relationship with Pep Guardiola. He’s scuttled off into retirement, showing his true moral compass by backing City when they were found overwhelmingly guilty despite saying in the past he’d walk away if such a thing were proven. Now we have Arteta versus Enzo Maresca, a man who has already decided his tenure there is likely to be short, so has taken to wearing outfits in order to audition for Guy Ritchie’s new Netflix special about geezers and wide-boys who are gentlemen in country houses who ride horses and love the rough and tumble of the good old days on the streets but wear a monocle while doing the violence and their wife is always called Cassie or something.

Anyway, let’s see what the manager says at his press conference later, which we’ll cover on Arseblog News in the afternoon.

Elsewhere, I know I mentioned it on the Arsecast yesterday, but I wanted to point you in the direction of the Arseblog gift guide, which could take some of the hassle out of your Christmas shopping. There’s Arsenal-related merchandise from all kinds of fantastic independent creators (and some official ones too), and you can find it here – https://gifts.arseblog.com/

A big shout to Andrew Allen for putting this together and compiling it, along with tech help from Tom and our friend @bootifulgame.

Finally for today, I just wanted to provide a little health update. After what feels like an interminable wait, I got results of scans/biopsies yesterday, and the news is that there was nothing more going than they initially thought. So, in context that feels like good news despite the obvious fact the overall diagnosis remains a load of shit I could really do without.

However, I can’t even begin to explain the relief of knowing. Like with anything, the absence of information creates a vacuum, and regardless of how hard you try to stay busy and to distract yourself, your brain tries to fill the gap. I don’t know if my brain is particularly unique, but there were times when that filling in was very, very dark, which becomes increasingly difficult to shake off as the days goes on and you’re waiting and waiting for info.

I now have a date for the first chemo session and everything goes from there. As I said in my initial update about this, I’m going to be around as much as I can be because I need the normality, but if there are some days in December etc when I’m not, that’s probably why. I definitely won’t be on tropical island in a hammock, but maybe that’s something to aim for when all this over.

Again, thank you all so much for your messages, they’ve really helped me over these last few weeks. To know so many people are in my corner, so to speak, has kept me positive when my silly brain went to those places I wish it hadn’t. Anyway, we have clarity now, let’s get on with it!

Right, I’ll leave it there for today. Have a great Friday folks, and for some extra reading, here’s Tim’s column on the evolution of Arsenal’s build-up this season.

#1642. Sunderland vs. Tottenham Hotspur - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 12:19, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 20:45

Separated by eight places in the Premier League table, 18th-placed Sunderland welcome mid-table Tottenham Hotspur to the Stadium of Light in matchweek 12.

The Black Cats have found greater defensive balance in recent weeks to sit inside the bottom three on goal difference alone, offering encouragement ahead of facing Roberto De Zerbi's men, who have won four of their last five matches.

Sunderland continue to struggle for victories this season, but the Wearside outfit's recent results suggest that Regis Le Bris intends to address their underwhelming start by strengthening their defensive foundations.

Le Bris's men collected four points at the start of the campaign before suffering four consecutive defeats, during which the Mackems conceded at least twice against Arsenal, Manchester City, Brighton & Hove Albion and Bournemouth.

Having failed to score in three of those four defeats, the Black Cats' problems at both ends of the pitch were laid bare.

Shutting out Leeds United, however, began a sequence in which Sunderland have kept three clean sheets in four matches, although their only Premier League victory during that period remains the 1-0 success over Chelsea at the start of the month.

Nonetheless, those shutouts suggest that Le Bris intends to repair his leaky defence before turning his attention to a misfiring attack.

That approach could prove useful when Spurs visit Wearside this weekend, with De Zerbi's men occasionally struggling against opponents content to surrender possession and frustrate them.

Sunderland's counter-attacking approach troubled Chelsea three weeks ago, and De Zerbi's men will hope to avoid the pitfalls that befell the Blues in that early-November encounter.

The North Londoners arrive buoyed by four victories in their last five matches, including three clean sheets, while the absence of European commitments has given them a full week to prepare.

That should benefit the 10th-placed visitors, although the joint-lowest scorers in the top half must deliver a strong away performance to climb the standings, with the capital club just three points behind fifth-placed Bournemouth.

Spurs could finish the weekend in the Europa League position currently occupied by the Cherries, although that would require Marco Rose's men to slip up and Brentford, Leeds, Chelsea and Everton all to fail to win.

Sunderland have several absentees this weekend: loanee Kevin Danso is ineligible to face his parent club, while Romaine Mundle (knee), Daniel Ballard (thigh), Habib Diarra (thigh), Granit Xhaka (calf) and Brian Brobbey (thigh) are sidelined; however, Dayann Methalie (illness) and Omar Alderete (knock) face late assessments.

Without joint-leading scorer Brobbey, the Black Cats will look to Enzo Le Fee to add to his three goals or another player to provide a match-winning contribution.

Although only Dominic Solanke and Jan Paul van Hecke have scored more than once for Spurs, the visitors can call upon Mohammed Kudus's creativity and ability to score from unlikely positions at the Stadium of Light.

Youngster Luca Jamie Williams-Barnett excelled on his full debut for the club, scoring and setting up Solanke's second-half strike against Ipswich Town to stake a strong claim for another start.

On the injury front, Xavi Simons (knee) and Wilson Odobert (knee) remain long-term absentees, while Mathys Tel (Achilles), Mykhailo Mudryk (ankle) and Savio (thigh) are unavailable in the short term; Tosin Adarabioyo (calf) faces fitness tests before Sunday, although Sandro Tonali is understood to have recovered from the illness that kept him out of last weekend's victory over Ipswich.

Roefs; Meunier, O'Nien, Mukiele, Reinildo; Sadiki, Ahoka; Hume, Le Fee, Talbi; Isidor

Tottenham Hotspur possible starting lineup:

Kinsky; Porro, Van Hecke, Senesi, Udogie; Tonali, Fernandes; Kudus, Maddison, Williams-Barnett; Solanke

Sunderland's three clean sheets in four matches suggest that Spurs will need patience, particularly against opponents whose counter-attacking approach has already frustrated Chelsea.

However, Brobbey's absence limits the hosts' attacking options, and the visitors' four victories in five mean we back them to edge a low-scoring contest.

#1641. Chelsea: ‘I didn’t expect João Pedro to fulfil his potential so quickly’ – former coach praises Brazilian’s progress

By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 12:28

In Brazil, Fluminense's youth academy is considered one of the best because of the number of players it has produced this century. And Xerem's greatest achievement was simultaneously having a generation of young players who reached the highest levels of world football.

All born in 2001, Joao Pedro (Chelsea), Luiz Henrique (Zenit), Andre (Wolverhampton Wanderers) and Matheus Martinelli (still at Fluminense) shared what was called the 'Golden Generation' of Xerem. Evanilson (Bournemouth), who is older and was born in 1999, was also in the team with them at some point in the youth system.

Three players who play or have played in the Premier League. One who was at the last World Cup. And another who won the Copa Libertadores with Fluminense and is still a starter for the team. A very rare feat that, for Gustavo Leal, who coached this generation for four years, was no coincidence.

The coach, recently runner-up in the Canadian Premier League with Atletico Ottawa, spoke with Trivela last week and explained the secrets to such a decisive generation.

Leal progressed from the Under-13s to the Under-20s in Fluminense's youth system and led this special group for four years. From the privileged position he held in this process, he understands that it was no coincidence and that the club, through its training methodology, plays a significant role in the development of these athletes.

'I strongly believe in the process and I do not think it is a coincidence that so many good players are in the same generation. It was a combination of the individual quality of the athletes and the good professionals they worked with. Xerem has many good people in goalkeeper training, in the physical area and in psychology' - he said.

The 40-year-old coach highlighted that several coaches had led them, such as Leonardo Ramos in the Under-13s (now in the Under-20s at Internacional), Thiago Macedo (who was Gustavo Leal's assistant in jobs in Mexico and Chile) and Marcelo Veiga, who currently coordinates the Xerem youth academy.

'This generation went through many good coaches. And this, combined with the quality that these players already had, allowed us to have such a large number of top-level players in the same generation' - he added.

When asked by reporters who surprised him most in this golden generation, Leal immediately chose Joao Pedro.

He then pointed out that it was not necessarily a surprise, but that what the striker has achieved is impressive. The 25-year-old was voted Chelsea's best player by fans last season and is maintaining that form this season.

'We always saw that Joao Pedro had a different kind of quality. Ever since he arrived in the Under-13s, we could already tell he was a special player. I think that, however optimistic we are and however much we work with the players to help them reach their full potential, perhaps we cannot imagine that this potential will be realised so quickly and at such a high level' - he commented.

#1640. Dundee manager Steven Pressley wanted to 'crawl under a rock and hide' after humiliation by Hearts

Published: 16:26 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:50 EST, 23 November 2026

Dundee manager Steven Pressley is nothing if not honest. Having taken full responsibility for his team’s 8-0 thrashing by Hearts on Saturday, he now admits that the experience left him wanting to ‘crawl under a rock and hide’.

You won’t hear him writing it off as a ‘bad day at the office’ or branding it a freak result from which he and his players would quickly move on. Dundee’s heaviest-ever home defeat in the league was an indignity that really hit their popular manager. And hit him hard.

‘It’s been a difficult 24-48 hours,’ said Pressley. ‘There’s been a lot of hurt, a lot of embarrassment. As you can imagine, at times I’ve wanted to crawl under a rock and hide.

‘It’s difficult on the back of such a disappointing result. But I will say this: I suffer a lot from vulnerability at times, but for some reason during difficult moments I seem to find strength from somewhere.

‘I don’t know if it’s from my family, from messages that I’ve received, from my reading. But I’ve had to show strength. I have to support the players. I have to make sure we navigate our way out of what was a really embarrassing moment.

‘We had a good meeting yesterday. We chatted a lot about the various aspects, and hopefully we can start responding to the disappointment.’

Dundee boss Steven Pressley says he felt hurt and embarrassed after losing 8-0 to Hearts

Defender Ryan Astley struggles to take in Dundee's heaviest-ever home defeat in the league

That process starts tomorrow night against Hibs, who suffered a humiliation of their own when they lost 4-0 at home to Dundee United on Saturday. Pressley says the immediate objective for his team is to go there with a better attitude than they have shown lately.

He had feared a setback coming for Dundee – ‘not 8-0 but a disappointing performance’ – because he had ‘sensed a little bit of subconscious complacency’. He felt his team had been over-hyped by outsiders on the back of a start to the season in which they won five of their 12 matches before the international break.

‘We’re nowhere near the levels that people keep telling us we are,’ he said. ‘We’re not a good enough team not to do the hard yards. Our whole strength has been built on the cohesion of the team, the unity of the team, the aggressiveness of the team.

‘And I think what Saturday did highlight is exactly what I’ve been saying. If we get lazy on the hard yards, we’re a very vulnerable team. We have to be at our absolute best to get results.’

He hopes the Hearts game will be ‘a reset moment’ that eventually helps his players to improve, but there are no guarantees from Pressley that they will shake it off at Easter Road tomorrow.

Asked if he expected a positive response from them, he said: ‘I don’t know. I know that they’re hurting. I know that they want to respond in the best possible way. That part I don’t question. I know how much it’s affected them.

‘But we’ve not had a lot of time. I just hope we can bring some pride back to the football club with the right type of performance.’

The good news for Dundee is that they are up against a team who have been hopeless in their own stadium recently. Second-bottom Hibs have lost nine of their last ten Premiership games at Easter Road and haven’t taken three points there since early April.

Supporters turned on the Edinburgh side after the defeat by Dundee United, but Hibs midfielder Jamie McGrath has dismissed the idea that he and his team-mates don’t enjoy playing in their own ground.

Jamie McGrath was in the Hibs side that suffered another defeat at Easter Road on Saturday

‘Personally, I always like playing at home,’ said McGrath. ‘I love the pitch, I love the stadium. It’s a big open pitch, which I think should suit us. But for whatever reason, so far this season we haven’t been able to capitalise on playing at home.

‘It’s hard to put your finger on one certain thing. Maybe just being more decisive in both boxes or probably conceding goals at crucial times in the game, like after five minutes on Saturday, we just give ourselves a bit of a mountain to climb.’

It looked like Marink Reedijk’s side had turned the corner when they followed up a rousing victory over city rivals Hearts in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final with a 4-0 win at Aberdeen in their last game before the international break.

So McGrath is hoping Saturday’s aberration was a blip. ‘We’ve been on a decent run the last month and probably the international break came at a tricky time for us. We were just kind of building momentum and had two good wins back-to-back against two good teams. It’s frustrating not to build on that.’

McGrath is unfazed by Hibs’ lowly league position and senses a chance to change that with three matches in the space of nine days against other sides in the bottom six.

‘It’s not something that we’re concerned about at the minute. It’s obviously not where we want to be. We want to try to get closer to that top six and this two-week period is quite crucial. If you put a little run together, you can boost yourself right up the league.’

#1638. Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the new season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

Joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The big Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

Half-hearted appeals for a penalty from Wissa, but Hayden Hackney did not do much wrong. Looks like we will be spared a first-half hydration break, despite it being a sultry evening.

Osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

Everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

Good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

Joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

Thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Big Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX

A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula

Your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#1637. Ipswich Town vs. Aston Villa: Unai Emery's side bidding to extend 42-year streak in Portman Road fixture

By Darren Plant | 27 Nov 2026 12:29

Aston Villa will be bidding to extend a 42-year streak when they face Ipswich Town on Saturday evening.

Unai Emery's side make the trip to Portman Road sitting in the bottom half of the Premier League table.

Furthermore, Villa are currently on a six-match winless streak, leading to Sports Mole arguing that Emery is no longer untouchable at the West Midlands outfit.

However, with a run of Ipswich, Everton and Crystal Palace to come in England's top flight, Emery will be optimistic that his team can turn around their fortunes.

Furthermore, Villa make the long trip to East Anglia looking to prolong a streak that has lasted more than four decades.

When the teams met in the 2024-25 Premier League campaign, they played out draws at their respective grounds.

Nevertheless, Villa earning a 2-2 draw on their travels extended their unbeaten streak at Portman Road to 10 matches.

Not since September 1984 have they suffered defeat at the home of the Tractor Boys, while Ipswich have incredibly only prevailed twice since that occasion.

That said, Ipswich have recorded draws in four of their last five home games against Villa, their only defeat coming in the 2017-18 Championship when they lost by a 4-0 scoreline.

Neither side has scored more than two goals in the last four head-to-heads, nor have they kept a clean sheet.

Newly-promoted Ipswich can move ahead of Champions League participants Villa this weekend.

If Gary O'Neil's side prevail by at least a two-goal margin, they will move ahead of Villa in the Premier League standings.

While Ipswich have collected seven points from five home fixtures, Villa have accumulated eight points from the same amount of away games.

However, neither team has won a game during November.

#1634. Aberdeen boss Mario Frick's heavy metal football is music to the ears of their long-suffering supporters

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026

As they embarked on the long journey home from Kilmarnock on Saturday night, Aberdeen supporters would surely have felt a little extra spring in their step.

If 2026 felt like it had been shaping up to be something of an annus horribilis, a 4-2 victory at Rugby Park undoubtedly lifted some of the gloom that had been hanging over the club these past few months.

Granted, a sample size of only one match under Mario Frick is very small. Nobody would be of a mind to get carried away with themselves just yet, especially given that Killie are easily the worst team in the league.

But there was enough in the performance, particularly during a first half which saw them score three goals in 30 minutes, to suggest that a brighter future could lie ahead under the new manager.

Aberdeen were aggressive, they played on the front foot, and they attacked with pace. Most of all, they were actually exciting and entertaining to watch.

Those were boxes they never ticked at any point during Stephen Robinson's time in charge. Robinson failed at Aberdeen and his team were routinely awful in terms of the quality of football they served up.

Mario Frick celebrates after a 4-2 win over Kilmarnock in his first game as Aberdeen manager

Ante Palaversa is back in the Aberdeen team after becoming the forgotten man of Pittodrie

Aberdeen striker Kevin Nisbet rediscovered the feelgood factor by scoring twice at Rugby Park

In the space of only 90 minutes, Frick did more to send a wave of positivity through supporters than Robinson ever managed to do in his eight months at the helm.

The shift in mood has been as profound as it has been instantaneous, with Frick's so-called heavy metal football music to the fans' ears.

Headlines of Super Mario were always likely to follow, but Frick and his players will face an altogether tougher examination when they take on Rangers at Ibrox tomorrow.

It is an intriguing contest on various levels, with Rangers unbeaten in 13 matches as Derek McInnes goes up against his former club once again.

Given that these teams met in the Premier Sports Cup only a few weeks ago, perhaps the greatest barometer of Frick's impact will be whether Aberdeen can pose more of a threat than they did at Hampden.

But what has changed? After such a turgid run of form that left players looking completely bereft of any confidence and cohesion, how was Frick able to generate an immediate improvement?

Speaking after the win at Killie, Frick was asked what sort of message he had given to the players given that time together on the training pitch had been fairly limited.

'I told them they should play like they did when they were young. In those days they didn't think about mistakes.

'They didn't think about anything negative. They played only to win, for fun.'

It was simple but refreshing. In an age of increasingly complex coaching jargon, Frick's message was intended to liberate his players – and it worked a treat.

Aberdeen went 2-0 up inside 12 minutes, with Kevin Nisbet scoring twice. The team looked free from the trauma of the Robinson era.

Even when Kilmarnock fought back and the game became more chaotic, Aberdeen retained enough attacking threat and collective belief to close it out.

It was a huge result. A defeat would have dropped Aberdeen to the foot of the table. Instead, they climbed five places and, more importantly, rediscovered a feelgood factor.

In his previous utterances, Frick was clear that goalscoring has been the central problem.

His previous teams at Vaduz and Luzern were known for their attacking output. At Luzern last season they scored 76 goals.

Aberdeen had managed only 12 in 12 league matches before his arrival. The early evidence suggests the players have absorbed the message quickly.

Frick's insistence on the basics – aggression, willingness to work, positive body language – appears to have cut through more effectively than more elaborate instructions might have done.

This is consistent with the picture painted by those who worked with him in Switzerland. Frick is not a rigid systems coach wedded to a single formation.

He has most often used a 4-4-2 diamond, but the shape is secondary to the mentality. High pressing to force turnovers, rapid counter-attacks, and a sense of freedom imbued to his players.

All of which makes tomorrow's clash at Ibrox all the more compelling. Aberdeen have lost their last eight meetings with Rangers in all competitions.

The previous two encounters this season, one in the Premiership and one in the Premier Sports Cup, were both settled by late Rangers goals.

The contrast in styles will be stark. Rangers are likely to control territory and force Aberdeen to defend for longer periods than they did at Rugby Park.

Frick's side will need to show that the freedom he has granted them does not dissolve into naivety when the opponent is stronger and more experienced.

The high press that worked so effectively against a struggling Killie side will have to be timed with greater precision.

The attacking play will require clinical decision-making in the final third. And the defensive structure, which Frick identified as the main area for improvement after Saturday, will be examined under more sustained pressure.

Frick has already spoken of aiming higher than mere survival. In a league which is always extremely tight in the mid-table, top six should be the minimum target.

That may have sounded optimistic a fortnight ago. But the win at Kilmarnock suggested Aberdeen have enough about themselves to be looking up rather than over their shoulders.

The squad still needs greater consistency and, in certain areas, greater quality.

But there is already evidence to suggest he can get a tune out of some players who either under-performed under Robinson or, in some cases, those who had been totally discarded.

Ante Palaversa would surely be chief among them. The Croatian midfielder hardly kicked a ball under Robinson and had become the forgotten man at Pittodrie.

Brought in to make his first league start of the season, his performance at Killie and the way he controlled things in midfield made his exclusion under Robinson look all the more bizarre.

None of this is to say that Aberdeen are suddenly a top-class football team. At best, they remain very much a work in progress.

Yet, crucially, Frick immediately has the supporters onboard in a way that Robinson never managed to do.

Frick and his players could yet be given a major reality check if they were to suffer a hefty defeat to a Rangers side unbeaten in 13 matches.

But there is belief and positivity in the camp at Pittodrie. Feelgood factors in football can often be fragile and often short-lived, but they are also real.

When players begin to play with freedom and confidence, results usually tend to take care of themselves.

Frick has not yet transformed Aberdeen. He has, however, given the players and the fans a reason to believe that a brighter future could lie ahead.

#1633. PEC Zwolle vs AZ Alkmaar - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 27 Nov 2026 12:54, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 13:35

Two of the Eredivisie’s most in-form sides meet in round 14, as PEC Zwolle face AZ Alkmaar at the Mac3Park Stadion on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts are unbeaten in their last five league matches, while the visitors are seeking a fourth consecutive victory in all competitions.

After losing three consecutive matches for the first time in almost a year around the start of November, AZ Alkmaar have responded with three straight victories. Their most recent success was a 4-2 win over Sparta Prague in Thursday’s Europa League fixture.

Leeroy Echteld’s men had to come from behind again in their midweek victory at epet ARENA and have now conceded the opening goal in each of their last six matches, often leaving them chasing matches more than they would ideally like.

Having scored 13 goals during their current winning run, De Kaasboeren appear to have rediscovered their attacking form as they prepare to visit a ground where they have already lost this year, suffering a 3-1 defeat to Zwolle in the third of last season’s three meetings.

AZ remain firmly in contention in what is shaping up to be an exciting title race, with only three points separating the top four in the Eredivisie table. The Cheese Farmers could end the weekend level on points with leaders PSV.

With two of their three league defeats so far coming on the road, where Sunday’s visitors are now five Eredivisie matches without a clean sheet, AZ certainly still have gears to find on their travels if they are to remain in the title conversation come the end of May.

PEC Zwolle finished just outside the bottom three last season, and their start to the 2026-27 campaign came as little surprise. They collected just four points from their opening eight matches, including a heavy 7-0 defeat to Feyenoord.

Taking over from interim Dennis van der Ree, Alex Pastoor made a winning start to life in the dugout thanks to a 3-1 win over Telstar, thanks to a Dylan Mbayo double and Ibrahim Cissoko’s early second-half strike.

The decision to part ways with Henry van der Vegt in October has since paid off, with Zwolle collecting 11 of a possible 15 points since his departure - the Eredivisie’s third-best return over that period.

Despite De Blauwvingers’ return to form, defeat this weekend could leave them just two points clear of the relegation zone ahead of their final three matches of 2026. Two of those fixtures are against current top-seven sides PSV and Fortuna Sittard.

Few teams are better placed to exploit AZ’s early-game struggles than Zwolle, who had opened the scoring in four of their previous five matches before their most recent victory, as well as in both of the last two meetings between the sides. Sunday's hosts will hope to strike early as they seek a third consecutive home league win.

Bulgarian international Filip Krastev has yet to feature for Zwolle this season as he continues to recover from an Achilles injury.

Eighteen-year-old Givaro Rahajaan and Sherel Floranus remain out of contention for the home side, who, however, have Sherel Floranus back available.

Attacking trio Jizz Hornkamp, Weslley Patati, and Mexx Meerdink are all unavailable for AZ, leaving them short of options up front.

Elijah Dijkstra, Stije Resink, Lewis Schouten, and Kees Smit will also miss Sunday’s match, with Resink yet to feature since March.

Ro-Zangelo Daal’s influential display off the bench in midweek took his tally to two goals and three assists in his last two appearances, making him one to watch.

Schendelaar; Burger, Graves, Viergever, Van der Haar; Thomas, Fichtinger; Mbayo, Namli, Cissoko; Van Hooijdonk

De Busser; Chavez, Hoedt, Goes, Maikuma; Stengs, Koopmeiners, Kwakman; Daal, Kovacs, Oufkir

AZ are dealing with several injury setbacks, which should give Zwolle some cause for optimism.

That said, the visitors remain favourites to win, and we expect them to edge a close contest.

#1632. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

After the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK

Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s

💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7

Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34

Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

Alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

Aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

Doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

Mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

Other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

Incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

The teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes issues for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

Madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

Referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly new rules that will be good for the game.

A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

In last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

This is going to be a very tall order for Aston Villa, who look very different tonight to how they ended last season, up against a team of PSG’s calibre. Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

McGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

Moments later, good work from Maatsen out on the left earns Aston Villa a corner. Unai Emery’s side have made a decent start to this game. Buendia’s delivery into the near post is headed away by Marquinhos.

We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

Some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. Both sides emerge from the tunnel, past the trophies they won with the two captains carrying them out, and we are moments away from kick-off in Salzburg. Here is a reminder of how the sides line up tonight:

💬 " I am confident they're going to play today with the level we need" Unai Emery on the inclusion of João Gomes and Brian Madjo into Aston Villa's lineup. 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FCjBmGDcNo

Lucas Digne has only just swapped Aston Villa for PSG in recent days but he already comes up against his old teammates. He is on the bench for PSG tonight and could offer some good insight into Unai Emery’s side.

PSG forwards Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and both are on the bench for PSG tonight. As PSG close in on moves for Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, could Liverpool’s moves for Barcola and Mbaye accelerate in the next few days? Barcola has only recently returned to training after the World Cup and is joined on the bench by compatriot Ousmane Dembele. Maghnes Akliouche, who has joined PSG from Monaco this summer, starts tonight.

Brian Madjo is just 17-years-old but he starts up top for Aston Villa tonight against the Champions League winners, with Ollie Watkins yet to return after the World Cup.

“There is a lot of change but when you look at other clubs in England, there is a lot of change. What we have still is our main core, same manager, same methods and same desire to achieve more. A lot thought we reached our ceiling a few seasons ago and we proved them wrong. As long as we have that hunger to achieve more, Aston Villa fans can expect as much as possible.”

New Villa signing Alejandro Garnacho has been ruled out tonight as part of the concussion protocols.

Garnacho was signed from Chelsea last month and took a whack to his face in the recent game against BG Pathum in Thailand.

Tonight’s game will be refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but got turned away at the border.

Team news is in 🔒 #PSGAVL pic.twitter.com/yeKkyIKiHQ

What will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

Unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

“I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”

#1630. Opinion: Julian Ward has found a perfect attacker for Liverpool

Liverpool have been constantly upgrading their team over the last couple of years.

The Anfield outfit have spent well over £600 million on new players to try and improve their ranks.

And, while some of the deal that they've struck have worked out, some still need to prove their worth.

Indeed, the performances of Liverpool's squad as a whole have improved thanks to the appointment of Andoni Iraola but, it's clear that there are still some problems that need rectifying.

Whether the Reds need to sign back-ups or replacements for their starting XI, change is needed so that they don't fall too far behind their title rivals.

So, the perfect attacker now being found by Liverpool is rather exciting.

Liverpool's attack has been one of their main focuses when improving their squad.

The Anfield outfit have spent well over £300 million on attackers alone over the last couple of years but, it still seems like the club aren't fully happy with the options that they have at their disposal.

That is obviously a crazy statement to share as, just this summer, £123 million was spent on Bradley Barcola alone.

But, with how many players Premier League clubs buy every season, there's no wonder why clubs have to constantly spend to keep up with their rivals.

And now, thanks to an update from X account Mekteb-i Gala, who have 50,000 followers, it seems like another attacker has made his way onto Liverpool's shortlist.

"EXCLUSIVE | PSG, Manchester City, Liverpool, Atletico Madrid, Como and Juventus are monitoring Yunus Akgün in every match," they wrote.

"They are in the process of gathering information on the player."

Yunus Akgun could be an unreal back-up option for Liverpool

Akgun is almost certainly a player that most Liverpool fans won't have heard of.

The Turkiye international is a 26-year-old winger who contributed to 21 goals across all competitions for Fenerbahce last term.

He's also had previous experience of English football as he spent the 2023-24 campaign on loan to Leicester in the Championship.

Unfortunately, his time in England didn't pan out as well as he would have hoped as he only contributed to six goals in the 29 games that he featured in.

Obviously, since most of his career has been spent in Turkiye, he probably wouldn't be able to get straight into Iraola's starting XI but, since he can play as a number 10 or a winger on either side, he could be an extremely useful back-up option for Liverpool to have.

These links are all just rumours at the moment but, of all the players who have been recently linked with Liverpool, Akgun feels like a really interesting deal for the Reds to explore, especially since they still need a back-up number 10 for Florian Wirtz.
